chapters.1: Legal Responsibilities, Site Roles, and Documentation
chapters.4: Hazardous Substances, Noise, Vibration and Manual Handling

bank.stem: Mid-task, heavy rain and fading light create conditions the written RAMS never anticipated. The supervisor says the RAMS is signed off so work continues as planned. What is the correct position?
o: Only the site manager may reassess the risk, so workers should carry on under the signed RAMS until he arrives and makes a decision on the work
A signed RAMS does not replace the ongoing duty to reassess as conditions change, so work should pause or be adjusted until the new risks are assessed
Work should continue, because a signed RAMS gives the supervisor legal cover for later changes in conditions that the document did not anticipate, such as weather
Work must stop for the day only if rainfall or light levels pass a fixed national limit set in law, otherwise the plan continues exactly as written
why: Anyone can and should stop work when conditions are unsafe, and supervisors should reassess promptly.
Sign-off does not cover conditions the document never considered.
No fixed national rainfall limit exists; the decision comes from assessing the actual risk.
bank.ex: Dynamic risk assessment means continuing to check conditions against the assumptions in the written document, and stopping to review when reality departs from them.
bank.cm: Treating the written RAMS as final, rather than a starting point that must be checked against real conditions.

bank.stem: Several workers report constant high workload, no say over deadlines and frequent last-minute schedule changes. The manager deals with it only through individual appraisals, calling it an attitude issue. Which statement best describes the problem?
o: Stress is a personal matter for each worker, and the employer's duty to assess risks does not extend to workload, deadlines or schedule changes set by the business
Stress only becomes a legal issue once a worker has taken more than seven days of sick leave, as the duty to act is triggered by recorded absence from work
Individual appraisals are the correct tool here, because stress is best understood as a question of personal resilience that each worker must manage
Work-related stress from demands and lack of control is a health risk to be assessed, and a pattern across several workers points to a systemic hazard
why: Employers must assess work-related stress as a health risk.
The duty to assess and act applies before absence occurs.
A shared pattern indicates a work-design problem that appraisals cannot fix.
bank.ex: Psychosocial risk factors such as demands and control should be assessed like other hazards, and several people reporting the same issue signals an organisational cause, not individual attitude.
bank.cm: Treating a pattern of work-design problems as a series of individual performance issues.

bank.stem: While removing a panel in a 1970s refurbishment with no asbestos survey, a joiner exposes fibrous grey-brown pipe lagging. A colleague says only white asbestos is dangerous and this looks brown, so work can carry on. What is correct?
o: Colour cannot identify asbestos, so presume it is present: stop work, keep others away, and report it so a competent person can arrange sampling
Lagging of this age does not contain asbestos, so the joiner can bag it as ordinary waste and simply notify the client about it after the shift ends
Brown asbestos is the lower-risk type, so work may continue in a disposable mask while the lagging is dampened and the loose fibres are bagged up
Only blue and brown asbestos are dangerous, so it is safe to proceed unless a later test confirms that one of those types is present in the sample
why: Pipe lagging of this period commonly contains asbestos, so it must be presumed present and never disposed of as ordinary waste.
Brown asbestos (amosite) is among the most hazardous types, and disturbed lagging must not be cleaned up by unprotected workers.
All asbestos types cause fatal disease, and work must stop before testing rather than carry on until a result arrives.
bank.ex: Material that may contain asbestos must be presumed to do so until analysis proves otherwise, and the discovery procedure is to stop, isolate the area and report, not to judge it by eye.
bank.cm: Judging whether a material contains asbestos, or which type, by its colour or appearance instead of presuming it until analysis proves otherwise.

bank.stem: A welder joins mild steel inside a large workshop with the doors open. The employer sees no need for extra controls, as no chromium or other toxic metals are involved. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Controls are needed only for stainless steel or galvanised work, because those metals produce the toxic fumes that welding regulations are aimed at
Open doors and the building's size give adequate general ventilation, since the fume from mild steel is only a nuisance rather than a serious health hazard
A disposable dust mask worn by the welder is enough, because the fume particles from mild steel are larger than those from stainless steel welding
Mild steel welding fume can cause lung cancer, so extraction at the weld is expected and RPE may still be needed for exposure the extraction cannot remove
why: Controls are needed for all welding fume, not just fumes from specific alloys or coatings.
Mild steel fume is a recognised carcinogen risk, and general ventilation does not reliably keep exposure low enough.
Welding fume particles are very fine, and a basic dust mask is not suitable protection.
bank.ex: HSE treats all welding fume, including mild steel, as a cause of cancer, and general ventilation alone is not enough indoors, so local exhaust ventilation is needed with RPE as back-up where required.
bank.cm: Believing that welding fume is only harmful when the metal being welded is a special alloy or has a coating.

bank.stem: A floor layer reports red, cracked skin on his hands after weeks of using a solvent-based adhesive. The manager proposes issuing gloves and barrier cream. What should the COSHH process lead the manager to do?
o: Gloves and barrier cream are enough because they stop skin contact, so the assessment can stay as written and no checks are needed for colleagues
Move this one worker to other tasks permanently, since the dermatitis shows a personal sensitivity and the adhesive remains safe for the rest of the team
Switch to any water-based product without further checks, because water-based adhesives are exempt from COSHH when they contain no solvents at all
Review the assessment and look first to substitute a water-based adhesive, keeping controls and regular skin checks for all users
why: Protective items sit below elimination and substitution, and the report shows the existing controls have failed.
Removing the affected person does not address the hazard, and others can develop the same condition.
Water-based products may still be hazardous, so the substitute needs its own assessment under COSHH.
bank.ex: COSHH requires removing or substituting the hazard where reasonably practicable before relying on protective items, and symptoms signal that the assessment and health surveillance need review.
bank.cm: Jumping to gloves and creams without first asking whether a less hazardous product could do the job.

bank.stem: Look at how workers get into and out of this trench. The foreman says the shoring makes entry safe. What is the main weakness in the access arrangement?
o: Ladders are unsuitable for supported trenches, so workers should climb out using the cross-struts of the shoring as steps
The ladder angle is too steep and should be made shallower, so the climber has more room to lean towards the wall
A single ladder is not permitted in a trench, and every worker must have a separate ladder fixed at three metre spacing along the run
The ladder neither rises about a metre above the trench top nor is secured on a firm base, making stepping on and off unsafe
why: Struts are not designed as steps and climbing them risks slips and displacing the support.
The usual setting of about one out for every four up is the correct angle, and a shallower ladder would slip.
A single secured ladder is acceptable where risk assessment supports it, and no fixed three metre spacing rule exists.
bank.ex: Ladders into excavations must stand on a firm level base, be secured against slipping and extend at least 1 m above the landing place unless another handhold is provided.
bank.cm: Assuming that once a trench is shored, the way in and out needs no checks of its own.
bank.alt: Two workers in a trench lined with steel sheets and props; one is climbing a ladder that leads up to the ground beside the trench.

bank.stem: A painter sprays a solvent-based coating wearing a reusable half-mask fitted with gas and vapour cartridges opened last month and left on a cabin shelf. He cannot smell solvent inside the mask and says they are still working. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Cartridges must be changed to the manufacturer's replacement period and shelf life and stored as instructed; no smell does not prove they work
Cartridges last until the wearer notices solvent inside the mask, so smell is a valid change indicator provided the mask has passed its face-fit test
Leaving cartridges on the shelf makes no difference, because they only take up contaminants when worn, so replacing them on a fixed schedule is a waste of money
COSHH sets a fixed legal interval of one month for changing gas cartridges, whatever the task, so these are now overdue and must simply be swapped
why: Relying on smell is unreliable and means the wearer has already been exposed, so replacement must follow a planned schedule.
Opened cartridges can absorb contaminants from the air while stored, which shortens their useful life.
No universal legal interval exists, and the change period depends on the manufacturer's information and the assessed exposure.
bank.ex: Gas filters become saturated with use and exposure, so replacement should follow the manufacturer's schedule and storage guidance rather than the wearer's senses.
bank.cm: Judging a respirator cartridge by whether the wearer can smell the contaminant instead of following a planned change schedule.

bank.stem: A groundworks supervisor clears a corner of the site by burning offcuts of tanalised timber, plastic pipe and packaging in a drum, while the wind carries thick dark smoke toward nearby houses. He says the fire is small and timber is natural. What is the correct position?
o: Carry on if the weight burnt stays under the daily limit of the registered exemption, because the limit applies to any wood waste produced on site
Stop the fire: burning mixed waste is unauthorised disposal that can release toxic fumes and dark smoke, so segregate it and send it for lawful recycling or disposal
Remove only the plastic pipe and carry on, because timber is natural and burning it releases only carbon dioxide and water vapour into the air above the site and the nearby homes
Carry on if the burn is recorded in the site waste management plan and the smoke is not dark, because the plan authorises on-site disposal of waste
why: The exemption allows only untreated wood and plant material burnt where produced, not treated timber, plastics or packaging.
Tanalised timber is chemically treated and releases harmful fumes when burnt, so it is not covered by the exemption for untreated wood.
A waste plan records waste routes and cannot authorise burning, which still needs a permit or exemption and must not create a nuisance.
bank.ex: Burning treated timber and plastics is not covered by the limited burning exemptions, creates harmful emissions and a smoke nuisance, and waste should go to licensed facilities under the duty of care.
bank.cm: Assuming a small site fire is harmless because it is brief and the waste is partly natural, when burning waste is itself regulated.

bank.stem: A labourer falls about 3 m from a low scaffold lift onto firm ground. He is conscious and reports neck pain and tingling in his legs. A colleague wants to sit him up and drive him to hospital in a van. There is no further danger nearby. What is the best first response?
o: Call 999, tell him to stay still, and hold his head and neck in line with his body until the ambulance crew arrive and take over
Sit him against a wall to ease his breathing and give him a warm drink while a colleague fetches the van to save waiting for an ambulance to arrive
Roll him into the recovery position at once, because every casualty who has fallen should be placed on his side to protect his airway
Loosen his clothing and ask him to move his fingers and toes to find out how serious the damage is before deciding whom to call
why: Sitting him up bends an injured spine and a drink is unsuitable if he needs surgery, while a van journey risks serious further damage.
Moving a conscious casualty with a suspected spinal injury risks further damage, and the recovery position is for those who cannot keep their own airway.
Asking him to move can worsen a spinal injury, and delaying the emergency call wastes time that specialist care needs.
bank.ex: A fall with neck pain and tingling suggests a spinal injury, so the casualty should not be moved and the head and neck should be supported in line while emergency help is summoned.
bank.cm: Assuming that moving a conscious casualty to a more comfortable position or to hospital yourself is quicker and kinder than waiting for the ambulance.

bank.stem: A dumper with a rear camera, radar sensor and audible alarm reverses along a route that pedestrians use to reach the cabins. The driver reverses fast because the screen is clear and the alarm is sounding. Which statement is most accurate?
o: With a camera and radar fitted the driver has full all-round vision, so the alarm and the pedestrians' own care are all that the route needs for safety on the day
The audible alarm warns pedestrians adequately, so the route may stay shared, provided people on foot wear hi-vis clothing and stay alert near the dumper at all times
The devices need testing only at the annual service, since they are fitted by the manufacturer and so are not covered by a driver's daily checks on the machine
Such aids support but cannot replace good site planning, so reversing should be reduced and pedestrians kept apart, with aids checked in daily pre-use inspections
why: Cameras and sensors have limited fields of view and blind spots, and they do not guarantee that nobody is behind the machine.
Alarms are easily ignored on noisy sites and hi-vis does not stop a vehicle running into someone.
Safety devices should be checked for correct operation as part of regular pre-use inspections, not only at annual service.
bank.ex: Cameras and alarms have blind spots and can fail or be ignored, so the main control is to design out reversing near pedestrians, using the devices as added support that are checked each day.
bank.cm: Putting trust in cameras and alarms instead of removing reversing from routes where people walk.

bank.stem: A subcontractor starts a refurbishment by reusing the RAMS from a similar job at another building, changing only the address and date. The new site has an open lift shaft and occupied offices next door. Which statement is most accurate?
o: A reused document becomes valid once the manager signs it as reviewed, because the signature shows the earlier controls were judged adequate anywhere
The assessment must suit this site's own hazards and people, so adapt it to the shaft and offices and brief the gang before work starts
A generic assessment is sufficient when the gang has worked together before, since their shared experience covers the site-specific hazards it omits
A reused assessment is acceptable when the activity is identical, because the hazards come from the task and site layout only affects the permit to work
why: A signature does not make controls suitable for new hazards, and the assessment still has to reflect this site.
Experience does not replace a written assessment of the specific hazards, and others such as office staff are not covered by it.
Hazards and who is exposed depend on the location as well as the task, so the layout cannot be left to a permit.
bank.ex: A risk assessment must be suitable and sufficient for the actual task, place and people affected, so a document from another site cannot be adopted without review and communication.
bank.cm: Assuming that a risk assessment from a similar job can be recycled with a new address on the front.

bank.stem: A boundary tree is protected by a tree preservation order. To lay a drain, the excavator operator plans to cut through its roots 1 m from the trunk, saying only the branches and trunk are protected. Which statement is most accurate?
o: The order matters only if the tree is felled, so cutting the roots is fine provided the tree is left standing when the work finishes
Cutting roots is a prohibited activity that needs the planning authority's consent, so re-route the drain or obtain consent first and fence the protection zone
The site manager can approve the root cutting once an arboricultural contractor has walked the route and agreed the line of the drain
Roots can be cut freely because the order covers only the visible parts, provided the cut is made cleanly with a saw rather than the bucket
why: Damaging a tree is prohibited as well, and cutting major roots can destroy it.
Only the local planning authority can consent, and a contractor's agreement does not substitute for that.
The order protects roots too, and a clean cut does not remove the need for consent.
bank.ex: A tree preservation order covers cutting roots as well as felling and lopping, so consent is needed and the work should be changed or authorised first.
bank.cm: Thinking a tree preservation order protects only the parts of the tree above ground.

bank.stem: An assessment scores three risks: a loose handrail on a spare office stair at 4, cluttered cable runs at 8, and an open lift shaft with no barrier on a busy floor at 20. The manager wants the cheap, easy fixes done first. What is the best approach?
o: Close the shaft at the next weekly review, since a lift shaft is a permanent feature and the score is the same whenever it is dealt with
Barrier the shaft immediately, then work through the other risks in order of score, recording who will fix each one and by what date
Fix the handrail and cables first as quick wins, then plan the shaft carefully, since a high score means the work needs more preparation
Treat all three as equal priority and fix them in the order they were found, because the matrix gives an indication and not a ranking
why: A score of 20 means serious harm is likely now, and the risk remains until a control is in place, so waiting does not keep it unchanged.
Ease or cost of a fix should not outrank severity, and leaving the highest risk exposed while quick wins are done is poor prioritisation.
The purpose of scoring risks is to rank them so that those with the greatest potential for serious harm are controlled first.
bank.ex: Controls should be prioritised by the level of risk, so the most serious risk is dealt with first, and recording owners and dates ensures that remaining actions are completed.
bank.cm: Letting cost and convenience decide the order of actions, instead of the severity of harm and the number of people exposed.

bank.stem: A small fire starts in an electrical panel inside a 3 m by 2 m unventilated switch room. A CO2 and a powder extinguisher stand by the door and the alarm has been raised. Which action is soundest?
o: Tackle it from the doorway only if small, with the exit behind you, then leave and ventilate, as CO2 gas and powder cloud both endanger people in tight rooms
Step in, close the door to keep the gas concentrated, and empty the CO2 extinguisher, because CO2 smothers electrical fires without leaving residue
Discharge the powder extinguisher from inside the room, since powder is the multi-purpose agent that suits electrical fires and its cloud settles harmlessly within seconds of use
Stay inside until the fire is fully out whichever extinguisher is used, since leaving a live electrical fire alone lets it spread through cable runs
why: Closing yourself in with discharged CO2 risks asphyxiation as the gas displaces oxygen in a small space.
Powder clouds cut visibility and can be inhaled in a small room, and they do not settle harmlessly.
Staying in a confined smoke-filled room puts the person at greater risk than the fire, and they should leave if it is not quickly controlled.
bank.ex: In a small enclosed room CO2 can displace oxygen and powder can blind and choke, so any attack should be brief from the doorway with an escape route kept clear.
bank.cm: Assuming that the right extinguisher type for the fire makes it safe to use in any room size.

bank.stem: An electrician must fix trunking to a 2.6 m corridor ceiling. The job takes all morning, needs both hands and means lifting 15 kg lengths overhead. He proposes a stepladder, saying ladders are fine for short jobs. Which is the best approach?
o: Stand on a 500 mm hop-up without rails, as a fall from such a low height cannot realistically cause serious injury to a fit adult
Use a podium step or low-level platform with guardrails, because long two-handed work with heavy lengths suits a platform, not a stepladder
Work from the second step from the top with a colleague footing the ladder, since footing makes a long task acceptable here
Use the stepladder but come down every 30 minutes, which keeps each stint within the recommended duration limit for ladder use
why: Falls from low height cause many injuries, and an unguarded step offers no protection while lifting heavy items overhead.
The top three steps should not be used without a handhold, and footing is a last resort, not a control for heavy work.
Duration is only a guide, and restarting a timer does not change the unsuitability of ladders for heavy two-handed work.
bank.ex: Ladders suit light, low-risk work of short duration, whereas sustained two-handed work with heavy items calls for a platform with collective protection such as guardrails.
bank.cm: Choosing a stepladder because it is the quickest kit to hand without asking whether the task's duration and loads suit it.

bank.stem: A roofer's fall is arrested at the edge and the team lowers him to the ground within minutes, unhurt. His harness shows no visible damage, and the foreman proposes using it again next shift after a quick look. Which approach is correct?
o: Return it to service once it has been washed and dried, because a harness spreads its load widely and a single fall cannot weaken the fibres
Reuse the harness but replace only the lanyard's energy absorber, since the absorber is the one component that takes real load in a fall
Withdraw the harness and lanyard until a competent person has examined them to the manufacturer's instructions, and review the rescue plan
Reuse it if the stitching and buckles look sound, because a harness is retired only when its webbing is visibly cut, frayed or torn
why: Washing does nothing to restore strength lost in an arrest, and a competent examination is what decides reuse.
The load passes through the harness webbing, stitching and fittings as well, so every part needs examination.
Shock loading can damage fibres and stitching without any visible sign, so a quick look cannot clear it for reuse.
bank.ex: Equipment that has arrested a fall may be damaged internally, so it must be withdrawn and examined by a competent person, and the rescue plan should be reviewed to learn from the event.
bank.cm: Judging fall-arrest equipment by how it looks after a fall instead of withdrawing it for competent examination.

bank.stem: A tiler with a full beard, kept for religious reasons, must dry-cut porcelain tiles that create silica dust. The supervisor suggests wearing a tight-fitting FFP3 half-mask over the beard. What is the correct approach?
o: Pass a face-fit test with the beard in place and treat the result as proof, since a passed test shows the seal is good whatever the facial hair
Wear a second disposable mask over the FFP3 half-mask to close the gaps round the beard, which doubles the protection provided
Trim the beard along the mask's edge and then wear the half-mask, since only hair under the sealing line affects protection
Provide loose-fitting RPE such as a powered hood or helmet that does not rely on a face seal, and use water suppression or extraction too
why: Facial hair in the seal area stops a reliable fit, so a test result cannot make a tight-fitting mask safe over a beard.
Stacking masks does not seal the gaps and can make the fit worse, so protection is not doubled.
Hair around the seal area, including the beard line and stubble, still lets air leak and trimming does not give a dependable seal.
bank.ex: A beard prevents a tight-fitting mask from sealing, so loose-fitting RPE is the suitable alternative, while controls at source reduce the dust the worker is exposed to.
bank.cm: Believing a tight-fitting mask, a trimmed beard or a double mask can seal over facial hair, rather than choosing RPE that does not need a seal.

bank.stem: A client's office fit-out is programmed for 24 working days with a peak of 15 workers, but the contractors' own programmes total 620 person days. The principal contractor says it is under both 30 days and 20 workers, so nothing needs sending. Who must act, and why?
o: The client must notify the HSE in writing before the construction phase starts, because exceeding 500 person days alone makes the project notifiable
The principal designer must notify the HSE, because preparing pre-construction information makes notification a core part of that role under CDM 2015
The principal contractor must notify the local authority once appointed, because it takes over the notification duty from the client at that point
The principal contractor is right, because the 30-day and 20-worker limits must both be exceeded together before any project becomes notifiable to the HSE
why: The principal designer plans and coordinates the pre-construction phase but the notification duty belongs to the client.
The duty to notify rests with the client and the notice goes to the HSE, not to the local authority.
The 500 person-day figure is a separate, alternative trigger, so passing it makes the project notifiable even when the other limits are not met.
bank.ex: Under CDM 2015 a project is notifiable if it lasts over 30 working days with more than 20 workers at once, or if it exceeds 500 person days, and the duty to notify the HSE sits with the client.
bank.cm: Assuming a project is notifiable only when it breaches both the duration and worker-number limits, and forgetting the separate person-days trigger.

bank.stem: A crew must lay 90 concrete kerbs, each about 70 kg, along a new access road. The foreman proposes two labourers lifting each one with kerb dogs, saying that with two people the weight is shared. A vacuum lifter fitted to the excavator is available. What is the best decision?
o: Continue with two-person kerb dogs but rotate the pairs each hour, because sharing the weight and varying the people brings the task within safe limits
Have the labourers roll each kerb on its edge along the road to the trench, since dragging avoids the need to lift anything off the ground
Use the vacuum lifter but let a labourer steady each kerb by hand directly underneath, since the suction would hold even if the load swung
Use the vacuum lifter, run by a trained operator on clean dry kerbs, with everyone kept out from under the suspended load
why: Rotation spreads fatigue but does not remove the repeated heavy lifting, so the task still presents a high risk of back and hand injury.
Rolling and dragging heavy kerbs still involves awkward twisting and strain, and ignores the available mechanical aid that removes handling.
No one should be under a suspended load, and a swinging kerb or a lost seal could crush a person standing beneath it.
bank.ex: Mechanical handling removes the repeated heavy lifting at source, and the lifter only works safely when the kerb surface is clean, the operator is trained and nobody stands beneath the load.
bank.cm: Assuming that two people sharing a heavy load, or taking turns, is an adequate control when a lifting aid is available.

bank.stem: A new concrete ramp rises 1.5 m to a first-floor slab and has an open side edge. Barrow loads run up it, and the only protection is red-and-white barrier tape between posts. The supervisor says tape and a sign are enough because the drop is under 2 m. Which statement is correct?
o: Tape cannot stop a fall or a barrow, so guardrails with an intermediate rail and toe board are needed, as no minimum fall height applies
A barrier with two warning signs is acceptable if inspected every day, because inspection is what the Regulations actually require for open edges
Tape is acceptable under 2 m, but a harness must be worn by anyone pushing a barrow along the open edge of the ramp as extra protection
A top rail alone at the correct height is adequate, because toe boards are needed only where other people are working beneath the open edge
why: Inspection checks that protection is working, and it cannot replace physical edge protection that prevents a fall.
There is no 2 m threshold in the Regulations, and personal fall protection is not preferred over collective edge protection.
Toe boards also stop barrow wheels and materials from going over the edge, not only protect those below.
bank.ex: Edge protection must physically prevent people and materials from falling, and the Work at Height Regulations apply wherever a fall could cause injury, with no minimum height.
bank.cm: Relying on the idea that falls from below two metres are minor, so tape and signs can stand in for proper edge protection.

bank.stem: A young labourer says his foreman shouts at him, hides his tools and gives him the worst tasks, and he now dreads work and sleeps badly. Raising it with the foreman is not realistic. What is the most appropriate route?
o: Wait until a doctor formally diagnoses a condition, because an employer has no duty to act until illness has been certified
Ask for a move to another gang and say nothing more, because a transfer solves it without involving management or leaving any paper trail behind
Take it straight to the HSE, because it investigates individual bullying complaints and can discipline the foreman directly on site
Report it in writing, with dates, to senior management or HR under the bullying policy so the employer can investigate
why: Employers must act on the risk of harm from work-related stress and do not need to wait for a diagnosis.
Moving away leaves the conduct unaddressed, so others may suffer and the employer is never put on notice to act.
HSE does not investigate bullying and harassment, and it expects concerns to have been raised with the employer first.
bank.ex: The employer must deal with bullying and work- related stress, and a dated written report to someone above the foreman starts that process and creates a record.
bank.cm: Assuming that bullying is only a personal matter, or that you must put up with it until it damages your health.

bank.stem: Two cleaners are to use a building's permanent suspended cradle with a safe working load of 250 kg. A third colleague wants to ride along with a heavy toolbox, and the examination report and rescue plan are missing from the handover pack. What should the supervisor do?
o: Let the three ride together if each is trained, since the safe working load is a guide that applies to the weight of the tools alone
Start with two operatives now, since the cradle is permanent and fixed, and ask for the paperwork when the first day finishes
Rely on the harness each operative wears, because fall arrest makes the missing rescue plan and the weight of the load unimportant here
Hold the job until the examination report and rescue plan are seen, and keep people and equipment within the safe working load
why: The safe working load includes the people as well as the equipment, so a third person and toolbox could overload the cradle.
Checking that the cradle is examined and a rescue plan exists must happen before anyone is suspended, not after the work starts.
A harness does not replace a rescue plan or the load limit, and it cannot rescue a worker suspended after the platform fails.
bank.ex: Contractors should see the thorough examination report and the rescue plan before work, and the safe working load covers the people and everything else on the cradle.
bank.cm: Thinking that a permanent installation or a harness means the paperwork and load limit can be sorted out after work begins.

bank.stem: A mobile crane must lift a plant skid with no weight marked and set it behind a hoarding the operator cannot see over. The foreman estimates it from the skid's size and offers to wave the operator on from the front gate. What is the best approach?
o: Lift the skid a short distance first to see how the crane handles, then continue if the boom and outriggers appear steady.
Let the foreman wave the operator on from the front gate, since an experienced person's hand signals are enough without any training or radio.
Confirm the weight from documents or by weighing, check it against the load chart at the working radius, and use a trained signaller.
Add a generous margin to the foreman's estimate and rely on the crane's overload indicator to warn if the real weight turns out heavier.
why: A trial lift cannot reveal how close the crane is to its limit, and capacity at the radius must be established before the load is raised.
A signaller must be trained, positioned with a clear view of the load and landing, and use agreed signals, which a person at the gate cannot do.
A guess is not a verified weight, and the indicator is a last warning device that should not be used to find the load weight.
bank.ex: The lift plan needs a verified load weight to check against the crane's capacity at that radius, and a blind lift needs a trained signaller using agreed signals or radio.
bank.cm: Judging a load's weight by eye and trusting the crane's alarms to catch a wrong guess. PRACTICE TEST 10

bank.stem: A groundworks subcontractor sends an 18-year-old, in his second week, to lay kerbs on a principal contractor's site. His gangleader spends the day on another plot, and the site manager says the principal contractor will keep an eye on him. Who must provide the supervision, and how much?
o: The principal contractor, because it controls the site, so the subcontractor's own duty to supervise ends once the young worker has attended the site induction
Nobody specifically, because at 18 he is legally an adult and a signed training record shows he can work without close checking
The subcontractor, as his employer, must arrange competent supervision matched to his inexperience and the risk, frequent enough to check and correct his work
The subcontractor, but a weekly visit from the gangleader meets the duty provided he has been given written instructions for each task
why: A site induction does not transfer the employer's own supervision duty to the principal contractor.
Being an adult and holding a training record do not remove the need for supervision matched to inexperience.
Written instructions and an occasional visit are not supervision proportionate to a new starter doing risky work.
bank.ex: Employers must provide information, instruction, training and supervision for their own employees, and the level rises with inexperience and risk, so the principal contractor's general oversight cannot replace it.
bank.cm: Assuming the principal contractor's presence on site means a subcontractor no longer has to supervise its own inexperienced workers.

bank.stem: A subcontract electrician's foreman tells the principal contractor that a temporary distribution board in its control has a cracked, open enclosure. The principal contractor replies that it runs the site, so work will continue. Which statement about responsibility is most accurate?
o: The subcontractor becomes liable if its workers are hurt, since a concern raised out loud is a request and does not create a duty until someone is injured
Only the principal contractor is liable, because CDM 2015 gives it control of the site, so the subcontractor's duty ends once the concern has been reported verbally
Both hold duties, the principal contractor for the board and the subcontractor for its own team, so the foreman should keep them clear and escalate in writing
The foreman may isolate the whole site supply himself, because reporting a concern gives him authority to stop the other trades' work at once
why: Duties arise from the risk and exist before harm occurs, so waiting for an injury is a breach already.
A subcontractor keeps its own legal duties to its workers and cannot hand them to the principal contractor by reporting a concern.
Raising a concern does not give one subcontractor authority over other trades or the site supply, and an uncontrolled shutdown can create new hazards.
bank.ex: A principal contractor's coordinating role does not remove the subcontractor's own duty under CDM 2015 regulation 15 to plan, manage and monitor its work, so each is answerable for its part.
bank.cm: Assuming that because the principal contractor controls the site, a subcontractor's own legal duty to its workers is somebody else's problem.

bank.stem: A roofer on a bright summer day buys fashion sunglasses to cut glare and plans to wear them under his helmet while cutting tiles with a disc saw. A colleague says a UV 400 label makes them suitable. What is the best advice?
o: Keep the sunglasses, as UV 400 lenses meet the standard for outdoor eye protection and the helmet peak shields the eyes from saw fragments
Rely on sun cream and the helmet peak, because glare is a comfort issue and eye protection rules apply to dust, sparks and splashes
Wear safety spectacles marked to EN 166 with an EN 172 sun-glare filter, as fashion lenses are not impact rated and a UV label ignores fragments
Choose darker wraparound sunglasses, since a closer fit stops fragments reaching the eye and a darker tint gives better UV protection
why: A UV label says nothing about impact resistance, and a helmet peak does not stop fragments from the disc saw.
Bright light and UV are recognised eye hazards, and the cutting task still needs impact protection.
Fit and tint do not make a lens impact rated, and a shattering fashion lens can add to the injury.
bank.ex: Eyewear for outdoor cutting must give impact protection from fragments as well as glare reduction, which industrial sun-glare safety spectacles are designed and marked to provide.
bank.cm: Assuming that any dark glasses with a UV label count as eye protection for site work.

bank.stem: A fourteen-person site, including two women, has one toilet cabin with three cubicles opening off a shared room. The doors cannot be secured from inside and no cubicle has a bin. The manager says separate cubicles satisfy the rules. What is required?
o: Separate rooms are needed only once six or more women work on site, and until then a notice asking men to knock first meets the duty on privacy
A single shared room is lawful if the women may use the first-aid room, since the rules count toilets per worker and not who uses them
Partitions inside one shared room are enough on sites under twenty people, provided women get set times by rota and used items are flushed away safely
Separate rooms for men and women, or one-person rooms locking from inside, kept clean and lit, with a suitable means to dispose of sanitary dressings
why: The duty to provide separate or lockable rooms is not triggered by a headcount of women, and a notice does not give privacy.
The first-aid room must stay available for treatment, and the regulations address separation and privacy as well as numbers.
A rota does not create separate rooms, and flushing sanitary items blocks drainage and is no proper disposal.
bank.ex: Construction welfare rules require separate rooms for men and women unless each room is for one person with a door secured from inside, and women need hygienic disposal.
bank.cm: Counting toilets per head and forgetting that privacy, separation and sanitary disposal are part of the welfare duty.

bank.stem: A plasterer finishes a dusty shift and hangs his half-mask on a van hook with the facepiece coated in dust. He knocks the P3 filters on the wheel arch and plans to reuse them tomorrow, saying he will change them when they "feel blocked". What is the correct approach?
o: Blow the dust off the facepiece and filters with compressed air at the end of each shift, then hang the mask on the van hook to dry in the open air
Clean and dry the facepiece as the manufacturer advises, store it in a sealed clean container, and replace filters that are damaged, dirty, expired or hard to breathe through
Wash the filters under a tap each week to restore them, then refit them once fully dry, because a washed filter regains its original efficiency
Keep the same filters until the facepiece seal fails its fit check, as filters only wear out once the rubber seal on the face has worn away
why: Compressed air drives dust into the filter media and leaves the mask exposed to fresh contamination on an open hook.
Particle filters must never be washed, as water destroys the filter material and its efficiency.
Filter life is independent of the facepiece seal, and a blocked or damaged filter can leak long before the seal fails.
bank.ex: Reusable masks must be cleaned and stored clean to prevent contamination and deterioration, and clogged or damaged filters cause breathing resistance and face-seal leaks.
bank.cm: Judging a respirator by whether it still feels wearable instead of cleaning, storing and changing it by a routine.

bank.stem: A hired lifting beam is to carry a 3-tonne precast lintel on a mobile crane. The beam's plate is badly faded, and the lift supervisor says that as the crane chart allows 4 tonnes at that radius, the lintel weight is the only figure to check. What is the best response?
o: Check the beam's working load limit and examination certificate but ignore its weight, since accessories are included within the crane's rated figure
Accept the faded plate if the hire firm says verbally that it suits 3 tonnes, then count only the lintel against the crane chart figure
The crane's rated capacity covers whatever it lifts, so accessories need no marking provided the lintel is within the chart
Confirm the beam's working load limit is clearly marked and its examination is current, then add its weight to the load checked against the crane
why: Crane charts give capacity for the load on the hook, so the beam, slings and any hook block weight must be added by the planner.
Marking must be clear on the equipment itself, and the beam's weight is part of the load the crane carries.
Accessories have their own working load limits and marking duties, and the crane chart does not cover them.
bank.ex: Lifting accessories must be clearly marked with their safe working load and be examined, and their own weight and that of slings count towards the load the crane carries.
bank.cm: Checking only the weight of the item being lifted and forgetting the lifting accessories and their markings.

bank.stem: A designer must choose how to join steel stair stringers in a small plant room. Site welding would need fume controls. Which option best follows the hierarchy of control when she decides what to specify?
o: Specify a lower-fume welding process with a portable extraction arm, since this captures most of the fume at source and keeps the original design unchanged
Keep the welded design and require welders to wear fit- tested FFP3 masks with rotation breaks, because masks protect the people carrying out the work
Specify bolted connections so that no site welding takes place, then reassess the new bolting tasks, including fixing at height and the torque tools used
Keep site welding but open the plant room doors and fit a fan, since dilution ventilation lowers fume levels enough to make the original design acceptable
why: Substitution and extraction reduce the hazard but leave welding fume present, so they rank below elimination.
Respiratory protection is the last line of control and should not replace removing the task.
General ventilation is a weak engineering control and does not remove the hazard that design could eliminate.
bank.ex: Removing the welding task eliminates the fume hazard at source, and any new tasks created by the change must still be assessed.
bank.cm: Choosing a cleaner process or better extraction when a design change could remove the hazardous task entirely.

bank.stem: A contractor proposes rope access to replace sealant on a 25 m facade. The technicians would use one anchored rope plus a fall-arrest lanyard clipped to facade brackets, and the assessment gives no reason a second rope cannot be used. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Rope access is not permitted where scaffolding or a cradle is feasible, whatever the assessment says, so the proposal fails on the choice of method alone
Rope access can be acceptable after assessment, but it needs two separately anchored lines, trained technicians and rescue, so reject this proposal
A single rope is acceptable where technicians hold a recognised rope access certificate, because certification replaces the need for a second line
The lanyard clipped to the facade brackets counts as the safety line, so one anchored rope plus the lanyard forms an acceptable two-point system
why: Rope access can be used where assessment shows it is suitable, but the system must still meet its own requirements.
Training is required in addition to the two-line system, not as a substitute for it.
The safety line must be a separately anchored line that travels with the user, not a lanyard on facade brackets.
bank.ex: A rope access system normally comprises a working line and a separately anchored safety line, used by trained people with rescue arrangements in place.
bank.cm: Believing that a trained technician on a single rope with a lanyard is equivalent to a two-rope system.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The joiner says the platform is wide, level and standing on a clean floor, so it is as safe as anything he has used. What is the most significant problem?
o: The trestles are too far apart, so the boards will bend, and spacing them closer would make the arrangement fully safe for this kind of work
The stepladder is not tied to anything, so lashing its stiles to a trestle leg would be enough to make the set-up acceptable for the work
The platform has no guardrails, so fitting a top rail and toe boards would fix the problem, whatever else is standing on the boards
A stepladder stands on the trestle platform for extra height, making an unstable stack with a longer fall, so use a platform of the right height
why: The boards are supported at a sensible spacing and the main fault is the ladder stacked on top, which closer trestles would not correct.
Tying a ladder to a trestle does not stabilise the stack, since the base itself can still move and the extra height remains.
At about one metre high guardrails are not the main control here, and rails would not stop a fall from the ladder standing above the platform.
bank.ex: Placing a ladder on a working platform adds height and instability to a set-up designed for a fixed level, so the platform should be built or chosen to reach the work.
bank.cm: Stacking one piece of access equipment on another to reach a bit higher instead of choosing equipment of the correct height.
bank.alt: Inside a room being fitted out, a worker stands on a stepladder placed on a trestle platform, fixing to the ceiling while a colleague holds a board below.

bank.stem: A roofer works from a low platform 3 m above a concrete yard. His 2 m lanyard with energy absorber is clipped to an anchor at foot level, and the supervisor says the harness makes the job safe. What is the main weakness?
o: A 2 m lanyard is too short for fall arrest, so a longer lanyard on the same anchor would let the system stop him before he reached the ground
The foot-level anchor is satisfactory, but a second lanyard should be fitted because two connections would halve the distance he could fall in a slip
The harness stops a fall before he reaches the ground once the absorber is fitted, so the only gap is the plan to rescue him afterwards
The clear space below may be too small, since lanyard, absorber and harness stretch could let him hit the ground, so edge protection is preferable
why: A longer lanyard lengthens the fall, which makes it more likely he hits the ground before the system stops him.
Adding a second lanyard does not shorten the fall distance, which depends on lanyard length, absorber extension and anchor position.
Rescue planning matters, but the absorber lengthens the fall, so he may hit the ground before the system stops him.
bank.ex: A fall-arrest system needs enough clearance below for the lanyard, the absorber to extend and the harness to stretch, and collective edge protection prevents the fall altogether.
bank.cm: Believing that wearing a harness and lanyard means a fall will always be stopped, without checking the clearance beneath the worker.

bank.stem: A 2.5 m deep service trench will be dug 1.5 m from the edge of a live road used by buses and lorries. The foreman plans to use the support supplier's standard strut table for firm ground. What should be done before digging starts?
o: Have the support designed for the actual ground, groundwater and traffic loading by a competent person, with inspection at the start of each shift.
Wait until cracks or water appear in the sides before fitting support, as made-up road base stands unsupported while it remains compacted.
Use the standard table and add one extra strut level for safety, since traffic adds a small load that the table's margin already absorbs.
Use the standard table and rely on a weekly inspection to catch any movement, because the road structure carries traffic loads away from the trench.
why: Support must be decided and in place before people enter, since collapse can happen without warning.
A table for firm ground does not account for traffic loading or groundwater, and an extra strut level does not replace a design for the real conditions.
Traffic loads can reach the trench sides through the ground, and inspections are needed at the start of every shift, not weekly.
bank.ex: Support must suit the real ground, water and loads from adjacent vehicles, and HSE guidance expects a competent person to inspect it at the start of each shift.
bank.cm: Trusting a generic support table without checking whether traffic loading and groundwater are covered.

bank.stem: After a gang member is seriously injured, HSE investigates a site supervisor who knowingly ignored the agreed method. A colleague says magistrates can fine no more than 20,000 pounds and only the company can be prosecuted. Which statement is correct in England and Wales?
o: The cap applies in magistrates' courts, and the supervisor is protected as an employee, since personal prosecution is restricted to directors who control company decisions
A cap of 20,000 pounds applies in magistrates' courts, though the supervisor can be prosecuted and the case can be sent to the Crown Court for greater penalties
Fines are unlimited in either court, and an individual such as the supervisor can be prosecuted personally, facing a fine and up to two years' imprisonment
Fines are unlimited but fall on the company, while the supervisor risks only dismissal or a civil claim and imprisonment is reserved for manslaughter cases
why: The 20,000 pound cap is not the rule in England and Wales, and individuals at any level can be prosecuted for their own breaches.
The cap is wrong for England and Wales, where magistrates' fines are also unlimited.
Individuals can be prosecuted under health and safety law itself and imprisonment is available beyond manslaughter.
bank.ex: Duty holders, both individuals and organisations, can be prosecuted, and in England and Wales fines are unlimited with imprisonment of up to two years available against individuals.
bank.cm: Assuming health and safety prosecution is something that happens only to the company and that magistrates' fines are small and capped.

bank.stem: After a fall from a mobile tower, an HSE inspector asks the bricklayer who witnessed it to answer questions in private and sign a declaration of truth. He refuses, saying his answers could be used against him if his employer is prosecuted. Which statement is correct?
o: He may stay silent as he would under a police caution, because an inspector's questions are voluntary until a formal notice has been served on his employer
He must answer, but anything he says can be used against him in court, so his best protection is to give short answers and decline to sign
He must answer only if his employer's solicitor is present, because an inspector cannot question a worker without the agreement of the company
He must answer and sign, because an answer given under this inspector's power cannot be used as evidence against him or his spouse or civil partner
why: An inspector's power to require answers is statutory and does not depend on a notice, so the police right to silence does not apply here.
The statute prevents these answers being used against him, and refusing to sign the declaration is itself a failure to comply with the requirement.
He may nominate a person to be present, but the inspector does not need the employer's agreement and a solicitor is not a condition of answering.
bank.ex: Section 20 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act lets an inspector require answers and a signed declaration, but section 20(7) bars those answers from being used in evidence against that person or their spouse or civil partner.
bank.cm: Assuming that talking to an HSE inspector carries the same risk of self-incrimination as being interviewed under police caution.

bank.stem: A crew repairing a foul sewer cleans up with the van's alcohol gel before lunch. One man vomited and had diarrhoea overnight, but feels better and wants to return the next morning, twelve hours after his last symptoms. What is the best action?
o: Allow his return on lighter duties away from the sewer, because the infection spreads through sewage contact and keeping him from the sewer protects colleagues
Keep him off site until he has been symptom-free for 48 hours, and provide soap, running water and a clean eating area rather than relying on gel
Allow his return, as twelve symptom-free hours is enough once he uses the alcohol gel, since gel kills the viruses behind sewage-related stomach bugs
Keep him off site for 48 hours but accept alcohol gel as the crew's handwashing method, as gel is quicker and copes with visible dirt on the hands
why: He can still spread infection through shared surfaces, tools, food and the cabin, regardless of where he works.
Gel does not kill norovirus and twelve hours is too short, as people stay infectious after symptoms stop.
Gel is ineffective on visibly soiled hands and against norovirus, so it cannot replace soap and running water.
bank.ex: Stomach bugs spread easily by the faecal-oral route and alcohol gel does not kill norovirus, so exclusion for two days after symptoms stop and proper soap-and-water washing both matter.
bank.cm: Assuming hand gel and a few symptom- free hours are enough protection against stomach bugs in sewer work.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The operative says his visor, ear defenders and safety boots mean he has all the protection a petrol brushcutter needs. What is the most significant problem?
o: His ear defenders are clipped to a hard hat and will not seal against his head, so he needs foam earplugs worn instead for brushcutter noise
His hi-vis vest could snag in the cutting head, so it should be removed while he works with the machine beside the fence
His lower legs are bare, so thrown stones or the cutting head could injure them; he needs protective trousers or leg guards
His mesh visor is the wrong type for flying stones, so he needs sealed chemical goggles worn in place of it for the whole task
why: Hat-mounted defenders suit this task, and replacing them with earplugs would not address the visible gap in protection.
A close- fitting hi-vis vest is not the main hazard, and removing it would reduce visibility to plant working nearby.
A mesh visor is the usual face protection for brushcutting, and goggles would not give the same coverage against debris.
bank.ex: A brushcutter throws stones and debris at ground level and the cutting head can strike the legs, so legs need protective trousers or guards in addition to visor, hearing and foot protection.
bank.cm: Assuming that protecting the head, ears and feet means the whole body is covered when a machine throws debris at leg height.
bank.alt: A worker cuts vegetation along a fence line with a petrol brushcutter; he wears a helmet with visor and ear defenders, a hi-vis vest, gloves, shorts and boots.

bank.stem: A trench excavator has a tilt rotator and a bucket. A groundworker with a level staff stands beside the bucket as the cab is stationary, thinking the machine is not slewing. The operator then rotates and tilts the bucket in place. What principle best explains the risk?
o: The risk is limited to the tail swing of the cab, so the standard fence around the rear counterweight is enough to protect the groundworker
The risk is only present when the bucket is loaded, so a groundworker may stand beside an empty bucket if he wears a hard hat
The tool can swing and tilt without the machine moving, so the exclusion zone must cover the tool's full reach, and entry needs the operator's agreement
A groundworker is safe beside a bucket whenever the operator can see him through the cab window and has been told where he is
why: The danger here is from the attachment, which moves well beyond the tail swing area.
An empty bucket on a rotating tool can still strike or crush, and a hard hat is no defence against it.
Visibility does not remove the risk, because rapid unexpected tool movement can still strike a person who is within reach.
bank.ex: A tilt rotator moves the attachment independently of the body, so a stationary cab is no sign of safety and people must stay outside the tool's reach until the operator has grounded it.
bank.cm: Judging safe distance by whether the machine body is moving rather than by where the attachment can reach.

bank.stem: On a sloping site, runoff reaches a road gully protected by a silt-filter mat. The foreman adds a silt fence with its fabric simply laid on the ground across the flow path and checks it weekly. Which improvement is best?
o: Let silt build up against the fence, since a deeper layer filters finer particles and a weekly check is enough whatever the weather
Place the fence directly across the swale where runoff concentrates, because the biggest flow needs the biggest barrier to hold the sediment back
Trench in the fabric foot, run the fence along the contour, inspect after heavy rain and clear silt, and limit soil washing off at source
Swap the mat for a finer-weave fabric so no silt can pass, which makes extra measures upstream of the gully unnecessary on a sloping site
why: Excess silt reduces capacity and causes overtopping, and checks are needed after rain.
Fences are not suited to concentrated, continuous flow and are overwhelmed or undercut.
Finer filters clog quickly and cannot replace controlling soil loss at source.
bank.ex: Silt fences work when the fabric is trenched in and set along the contour, and they need inspection after rain, with measures that limit soil washing off at source.
bank.cm: Assuming a drain mat or silt fence will cope with any sediment, instead of keeping soil out of runoff at source.

bank.stem: Scaffolders stripping a scaffold beside a public footway stack 6.4 m tubes and loose couplers on the top lift to lower later. The tube ends project beyond the guardrail over the footway, and the stack sits at the access ladder. Which change best controls the risk?
o: Keep tubes inside the guardrail line, lash them in bundles and bag the fittings, then lower them as stripping goes on, not stockpile them
Pile the tubes at the ladder access, because it keeps them away from the edge and makes them quickest to lower at the end of the shift
Leave the stack as it is but cone off the footway beneath it, since the toe boards stop any tube or coupler from falling off the lift edge
Push the stack back until the ends clear the guardrail, and leave the couplers loose on the boards where they are within easy reach
why: A stack at the access blocks the way on and off the lift and creates a trip hazard in the escape route.
Toe boards do not hold projecting tubes or loose couplers, and cones do not stop an object hitting someone who walks past.
Loose couplers still roll or get kicked over the edge, and the stack still blocks the access ladder.
bank.ex: Keeping materials to a small, secured quantity inside the guardrails, clear of the access and the public, limits both the dropped-object and the trip hazard.
bank.cm: Stockpiling stripped scaffold materials on a lift as if the platform were a store.

bank.stem: At a plant yard wash-down area, the oil separator's high-level alarm sounds. The yard supervisor suggests flushing it through with hot water and a degreaser so the oil is pushed out into the surface-water drain. What is the correct action?
o: Carry on using the wash area and check it again at the next six-monthly inspection, since the alarm only warns that oil is near its limit
Skim the oil off the top with a bucket and tip it into the site's general waste skip, then reuse the separator without refilling it with water
Stop using the wash area, have a registered waste carrier empty it and refill it with clean water, and log the work and hazardous waste paperwork
Flush it with hot water and degreaser to disperse the oil to the drain, since detergent breaks the oil down so it does little harm to the watercourse
why: The alarm means the separator should be emptied right away, as continued use will pass oil through into the drain.
Oily waste is hazardous and does not belong in a general skip, and the separator must be refilled with clean water to work.
Detergents emulsify oil and stop the separator working, and the oil would reach the surface- water drain and pollute the watercourse.
bank.ex: An alarm shows oil or silt has reached its limit, so the separator must be emptied by a registered carrier, with oily waste treated as hazardous, and refilled with clean water before reuse.
bank.cm: Treating a separator alarm as a routine reminder, when oil that is not removed properly goes straight to the drain.

bank.stem: A fitter must hang cable tray in a plant room with 2.4 m headroom, where bare live busbars run across the ceiling. He plans a fibreglass stepladder, saying fibreglass does not conduct, and a colleague will warn him if his head gets close. What is the correct view?
o: Neither measure is adequate; work within reach should wait until the busbars are made dead or physically barriered so nobody can come into contact
The fibreglass ladder makes the job acceptable, provided he uses plastic-handled tools and takes care not to touch the busbars with his hands
The spotter is a sufficient control if he is competent, because a verbal warning gives the fitter time to move away before any contact
A shorter stepladder solves the problem, because keeping his head below 2 m leaves a clear gap to the busbars at 2.4 m
why: Fibreglass does not guarantee safety, because dirt, damp and conductive tools or tray can still bring him into contact or arcing range.
A warning cannot stop a slip or a long tray length touching live parts, so it is not a barrier.
Tools, tray and raised arms reach well above the head, so the busbars remain within reach.
bank.ex: Under the Electricity at Work Regulations live conductors that could cause injury must be made dead or guarded, and a fibreglass ladder or spotter does not prevent contact or arcing.
bank.cm: Relying on an insulating ladder or a lookout instead of making the live parts dead or inaccessible.

bank.stem: A site joinery shop's dust extractor hopper is full of fine sawdust, with fine dust coating beams and a grinder working nearby. A joiner says sawdust only burns when it is lit with a flame, so there is no explosion risk. What is the correct view?
o: Dust explodes only in factories handling flour or coal, so a small joinery shop need not worry about sparks near its dust
The risk comes only from an open flame, so banning smoking and naked lights is enough while the grinder keeps working
Fine dust suspended in air can explode if ignited, so clean regularly, control ignition sources such as grinder sparks and empty the hopper
A full hopper is safer than an empty one because the dust is packed tight, and compacted dust cannot catch fire
why: Wood dust is also combustible and can explode when dispersed and ignited.
Sparks from grinders and other sources can ignite dust cloud as well.
A full hopper holds fuel and can still smoulder or burn.
bank.ex: Fine combustible dust can burn very fast when dispersed in air and ignited by a spark, so housekeeping, ignition control and emptying collectors are needed.
bank.cm: Assuming dust is only a health problem and cannot cause fires or explosions.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. A concrete pour is under way. Which statement best identifies the most significant problem?
o: The boom is working too close to the operatives' heads, so the main hazard is wet concrete dripping into unprotected eyes, which goggles alone would solve
The operatives stand on reinforcement mesh, so the main hazard is tripping, which boards would fix since the pump operator controls any hose movement
The operatives are stretching the end hose out horizontally to reach the pour, so air or a blockage could whip it and throw them; the pump should be moved
The pump lorry is parked too far back, so the main hazard is the pump operator losing sight of the pour, solved by a second operator on a radio
why: Splash is a real but lesser risk than hose whip with the line stretched out.
Boards are present and the hose end moves with pressure surges that the pump operator cannot fully control.
Moving the pump closer is part of the fix, but the hazard shown is the stretched hose, not visibility.
bank.ex: The end hose should hang near vertical and be guided, never pulled out horizontally, because pressure surges can make it whip violently and strike or throw the handlers.
bank.cm: Focusing on splash or tripping while overlooking the risk of the delivery hose whipping when it is held out and stretched.
bank.alt: Two workers hold the end hose of a concrete pump boom over a reinforced slab during a pour, with the pump lorry behind them.

bank.stem: A kerbing gang will use petrol disc cutters for three weeks. The hire firm offers the standard model, or a quieter model of similar output for a small extra cost. The manager prefers the standard cutter and plans to issue ear defenders, calling this equally compliant. Which view is correct?
o: The choice should be made on hire price alone, since suppliers' noise data are unreliable and exposure can only be judged from site measurements
The two choices are equally compliant, because a high enough rated pair of ear defenders removes any difference in exposure between the models
Noise should be cut at source first, including choosing the quietest suitable equipment, with hearing protection covering only the exposure that remains
The quieter model matters only if the standard model is proven to exceed the upper exposure action value, since lower levels carry no duty to reduce noise
why: Suppliers must give noise emission data and it should guide equipment choice before work begins, not be dismissed.
Hearing protection is not a substitute for reducing noise at source, and attenuation in real use is less than the rating suggests.
The duty to reduce noise risk as far as reasonably practicable applies below the upper action value too.
bank.ex: The noise regulations require risk to be eliminated or reduced at source as far as reasonably practicable, which includes choosing equipment that emits least noise, with hearing protection as a later measure.
bank.cm: Treating hearing protection as the main noise control instead of first choosing quieter equipment and methods.

bank.stem: A fire in a half-built timber-frame block is put out, and the fire and rescue service hands the area back. Short of programme time, the manager wants trades back in at 7 am. What should be done before anyone is allowed back in?
o: Keep it closed until a competent person has checked the structure and temporary works and the fire risk assessment and alarms are reviewed
Re-admit workers once the area has been cleaned and dried, because soot and water are the remaining hazards and a structural check can follow later
Allow trades back on any floor the fire did not reach, since only the burnt area is unsafe and the fire service has already cleared the whole building
Restart when the insurer's loss adjuster has photographed the damage and approved a restart, because the insurer would otherwise refuse the claim
why: Hidden structural weakening is the main danger and must be checked before people return, not after.
Handing back the area ends firefighting but does not confirm the structure is sound, and smoke, water and damaged fire systems affect floors beyond the burnt area.
An insurer's approval is about cover and says nothing about whether the structure and fire precautions are safe.
bank.ex: A fire can weaken frames, props and floors and put out of action detectors and escape routes, so re-occupation needs a competent structural check and a revised fire risk assessment.
bank.cm: Believing that once the fire is out and the brigade has left, the area is safe to re-occupy.

bank.stem: An electrician isolates the lighting circuit for a staircase in an occupied office and locks off the breaker, keeping the key. He starts to replace a failed fitting while staff are still using the now- dark stairwell. What has he missed?
o: Nothing, because once the circuit is locked off and he holds the key the electrical risk is controlled, and the stairwell lighting is the building manager's problem alone
A warning notice at the breaker and another at the foot of the stair should replace the lock, because notices tell staff and the key can stay in the cabinet
He should have warned the occupants beforehand and arranged temporary lighting or closed the stair, and he still needs to prove the fitting dead at the point of work
He should tell staff to use the lift instead and rely on the wall switch being off as proof that the fitting is dead, rather than testing it
why: Isolation creates a new hazard for occupants that the person isolating must warn about and help control, beyond the electrical lock-off.
Notices are easily missed and are not a substitute for keeping the isolation under the control of the person working.
A wall switch off does not prove the fitting is dead, and sending people to a lift does not address safe lighting for the stair.
bank.ex: Safe isolation requires notifying those affected by the loss of supply and controlling the new hazard it creates, while locking off and then proving the fitting dead before touching conductors.
bank.cm: Thinking safe isolation is only about protecting the electrician, and forgetting the people who lose lighting or other services when the circuit goes off.

bank.stem: Digging a drainage trench in a former wartime dock area, an excavator bucket uncovers a rusty, finned metal cylinder about a metre long. The operator wants to lift it out and set it aside until the engineer arrives. What is correct?
o: Tap it with a spade to hear whether it rings hollow, since an empty casing is harmless scrap that can go in a skip
Photograph it, keep digging at the far end of the site, and ask the client to arrange a survey by the end of the week
Stop work, leave it untouched, move everyone well back and alert the police, treating it as live until experts say otherwise
Lift it carefully clear of the trench and cordon off the pile, because a slow, smooth lift is safer than leaving it beside an unstable trench wall
why: Striking an unknown item is dangerous, and it is impossible to tell from outside whether it is empty or fused.
Carrying on work and waiting days leaves people near a possible explosive, when the area should be cleared at once.
Lifting or moving a suspect item can set it off, and the bucket and trench wall should not be disturbed further.
bank.ex: Suspected unexploded ordnance can be unstable after decades underground, so it must not be moved or disturbed and the area must be cleared pending specialist disposal.
bank.cm: Treating a rusty old object as scrap or as someone else's problem instead of as possibly live ordnance.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The driver says it is only a two-minute run to the stockpile and the track is level and dry. What is the most significant problem?
o: People ride on a machine built only for the driver, so a bump or braking could throw them off or under the wheels
The skip should be raised slightly while travelling, so that the driver has a clearer view of the track surface ahead of him
The pallet of kerbs on the verge is too close to the track, so vibration from the passing dumper could bring the whole stack down
No banksman is walking ahead of the machine, so the driver cannot be guided along what is a straight and otherwise clear stretch of track
why: Travelling with the skip raised reduces stability and is not good practice; it is also not what makes this scene dangerous.
The stack is neat, set back from the track and not the most significant hazard in the picture.
A banksman is not the key issue on a clear, level track; the bigger fault is people on the machine.
bank.ex: Site dumpers are not built to carry passengers, and anyone riding on the skip is at risk of falling and being run over or crushed.
bank.cm: Assuming a short journey on firm, level ground makes it acceptable to let colleagues ride on plant not built for passengers.
bank.alt: A site dumper drives along a gravel track carrying a driver and two other workers sitting on the front of the skip.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The worker is correctly wearing high-visibility clothing as the blue sign requires. What is the most significant problem being missed?
o: The only problem is that the mandatory sign should be green rather than blue, as green is the colour used for signs requiring protective equipment
Nothing is wrong, because high-visibility clothing makes the worker visible enough to drivers to cross the vehicle route wherever he chooses
The red sign is a warning that vehicles may be present, so the worker is free to cross at this point provided he takes care and watches for traffic
He is crossing where a prohibition sign bars pedestrians instead of using the marked crossing, so obeying the PPE sign does not excuse ignoring the route restriction
why: Blue circles are the correct colour for mandatory signs; green is for safe conditions and emergency information.
Hi-vis makes a person more visible but does not make unsegregated crossing safe or permitted.
A red circle with a bar is a prohibition, not a warning; warnings are yellow triangles.
bank.ex: The two signs require different things: the mandatory sign is about PPE and the red prohibition sign is about where pedestrians may go, so compliance with one does not excuse breaching the other.
bank.cm: Treating compliance with one sign, such as the hi-vis requirement, as permission to ignore another sign about route restrictions.
bank.alt: A worker in a hi-vis jacket walks along a site haul road past a red circular sign showing a crossed-out pedestrian and a blue sign showing a hi-vis vest; a marked crossing is nearby.

bank.stem: Workers cutting concrete in a confined yard wear FFP1 disposable masks because 'any dust mask is better than nothing'. The dust is respirable crystalline silica. Which statement is most accurate?
o: FFP1 is the highest rating available, so it is the best choice for silica and no higher class is needed for cutting work such as this in a yard
Any FFP mask is equally suitable for any dust, because the number printed on it measures comfort and fit rather than filtering efficiency or the level of protection
The mask must be rated for the hazard, and silica needs a higher class than FFP1, so a wrongly rated mask gives false confidence without adequate filtration
A mask is unnecessary if the cutting is done outdoors, because the dust disperses in open air and exposure stays below any workplace exposure limit
why: FFP1 is the lowest of the three classes.
The class indicates filtering efficiency and must match the hazard.
Outdoor work still exposes workers to silica, which needs controlling at source and suitable RPE.
bank.ex: RPE must match the contaminant and exposure level; FFP1 filters far less than the protection required for silica, so it can leave workers inadequately protected while believing otherwise.
bank.cm: Believing that any respiratory protection beats none, without checking its rating against the hazard.

bank.stem: Edge protection on a flat roof has a single top rail at 900 mm and no intermediate rail or mesh, and the supervisor says the top rail is the main protection so that is sufficient. Which statement is most accurate?
o: A toe board alone can replace the intermediate rail, because it blocks the same gap beneath the top rail and stops anything falling over the edge
Only the missing intermediate rail is a problem, since top rails may be any height from 800 mm upwards where the roof is flat and the work is short
900 mm meets the requirement for a main guardrail on a flat roof, and a single top rail is sufficient where the edge is some distance from the work area
The top guardrail should be at least 950 mm, and with no intermediate rail the gap exceeds the 470 mm maximum, so both height and gap are deficient
why: A toe board stops objects rolling off; it does not fill the gap between the top rail and the toe board.
The top rail height requirement is 950 mm, so the height is also deficient.
The minimum is 950 mm and a gap greater than 470 mm is not allowed.
bank.ex: Edge protection needs a main guardrail at least 950 mm high, an intermediate guardrail or equivalent so no gap exceeds 470 mm, and a toe board of at least 150 mm.
bank.cm: Checking only that a top rail exists, without verifying its height and the size of the gaps beneath it.

bank.stem: In a heatwave, a new starter begins heavy hod carrying on a flat roof. Colleagues advise him to drink only when thirsty and rely on sun cream alone. Which plan best controls the risks?
o: Experienced colleagues can skip the precautions, and only the new starter needs acclimatising, as long as the hottest hours are worked at full pace
Build up his workload gradually, give shade and water before thirst, move heavy tasks to cooler hours, and add covering clothing and sun cream
Salt tablets and fizzy drinks at breaks keep him going, because thirst is a reliable signal and replacing salt matters more than regular water
Sun cream applied each morning is enough, because heat illness is mainly a skin problem and clothing or workload changes would only slow the job
