Treat the certificate as a starting point, then check the firm's experience, resources and proposed method for this particular chimney job
why: HSE does not treat membership as a sufficient assessment of organisational capability for the particular work.
Capability is judged on relevant skills, resources and planning, not on having completed an identical job.
Competence must be checked before appointment, since waiting until work has started leaves the risk uncontrolled.
bank.ex: Accreditation shows a general health and safety standard, but HSE says it is not on its own enough to judge a firm's capability for a specific project.
bank.cm: Assuming that a valid accreditation certificate settles whether a subcontractor can safely carry out this specific job.

bank.stem: Scaffolders plan to hang a working platform from steel beams across a stairwell void, copying a layout from a guide for standard freestanding scaffolds. The decorators want it tomorrow. Which requirement applies to this scaffold?
o: The guide layout is enough provided the tube and fitting quantities match and a trained scaffolder erects it, with no separate design needed
A competent person must produce a specific design and plan, including whether the beams can carry the load, and it must be inspected before first use
The building owner's verbal agreement that the beams are sound is enough, with any design check made once the platform is up and in use
Design is needed only if the load exceeds general-purpose loading, and the first inspection can then wait until seven days after use begins
why: A guide for freestanding scaffolds does not cover a platform hung from the structure, so a specific design is needed.
The supporting structure must be checked by a competent person as part of the design before the scaffold is used, not after.
A non-standard scaffold needs design whatever the load, and inspection is required after erection and before first use.
bank.ex: A hung scaffold is outside standard configurations, so it needs bespoke design and a plan, and a competent person must inspect it after erection and before it is used.
bank.cm: Assuming a scaffold can be built from a standard guide when it hangs from the structure instead of standing on the ground.

bank.stem: On a wet plot, a generator-fed saw runs through a 30 mA RCD adaptor, which the electrician tested with its button once on Monday. On Wednesday it trips every time the saw starts, and the operator wants to plug straight into the generator's unprotected socket. What is the correct approach?
o: Stop using that saw, treat the tripping as a fault for a competent person to find, and press the RCD test button before every future use
Use the unprotected socket for this cut only, as Monday's test showed the RCD works and the tripping is just nuisance from start-up surge
Swap to a 100 mA RCD that ignores the start-up surge, because it still protects people from shock while giving fewer unwanted trips
Reset it after the saw cools and test the RCD weekly, since the periodic combined test already covers the day-to-day checks
why: A trip is a sign of a fault, a test earlier in the week proves nothing about today, and bypassing the RCD removes the protection.
Higher-rated RCDs protect against fire and do not protect people from shock, and the underlying fault would remain.
Repeatedly resetting hides a fault, and the user test button check is needed before each use as well as periodic testing.
bank.ex: An RCD that trips is a warning of a fault, it must never be bypassed, and the test button should be used before each use rather than once a week.
bank.cm: Treating a tripping RCD as a nuisance to be bypassed or swapped and not as a sign of a real electrical fault.

bank.stem: Ear defenders hang in a van, crushed under tools. Many have hardened, cracked cushions and loose headbands, and the stores log records only each pair's issue date. What must the employer do?
o: Nothing yet, because defenders stay effective until a muff splits and the issue date shows they are within a normal two- year life
Swap everyone to disposable foam plugs, since plugs cannot wear out and so need no storage, checking or replacement
Make each worker responsible for storing and replacing their own pair, since personal issue passes the maintenance duty to the wearer
Provide suitable storage, check condition regularly, and clean or replace worn parts or whole defenders at the maker's intervals
why: Hardened cushions and slack bands reduce attenuation before any visible split, and there is no fixed two-year rule.
Plugs still need correct fitting and hygienic storage, and the choice must match the noise level.
The employer remains responsible for maintaining and replacing PPE it provides.
bank.ex: PPE regulations require employers to maintain, clean or replace PPE and to provide accommodation for it when not in use, because worn cushions and bands lose protection.
bank.cm: Thinking PPE is only the employer's concern on the day it is issued.

bank.stem: Fitters hang a one-tonne lever hoist from a beam to raise a 400 kg pipe spool. The lever is stiff, so one slides a scaffold tube over the handle, and the apprentice offers to ride the spool upwards to steady it. Which statement is correct?
o: The apprentice may ride it if he is clipped to the hook, but the tube must come off since only the lever should operate the hoist
Both are acceptable provided the beam has been checked, because the spool is well below the hoist's rated load, and the apprentice holds the chain
Neither is acceptable: a stiff lever signals an overload or fault to check, and nobody may ride a load on equipment not designed to lift people
The tube is acceptable since the spool is well below the one-tonne rating, but the apprentice must stay clear and use a tag line
why: Clipping a person to a hoist hook does not make it a safe means of lifting people, as the equipment is not designed or examined for that.
Extending the lever can overload the hoist whatever the weight, and riding a load is never safe with equipment not designed for people.
Extending the lever defeats the hoist's design and can mask a fault or overload, even with the load well within its rating.
bank.ex: An extended lever can overload the hoist and hide a fault, and lifting equipment not marked for people must never carry anyone.
bank.cm: Assuming that a load well below the rated capacity allows any improvised leverage or a person to ride along.

bank.stem: A 4.8 m high flat-roof edge is reached by a ladder whose foot is 0.6 m from the wall and sits on a slumped mound of spoil. Its top is level with the coping. Which set of corrections makes it safe to climb?
o: Move the foot about 1.2 m out onto firm level ground and use a longer ladder rising at least 1 m or three rungs above the coping
Move the foot about 1.2 m out, lay a plank on the spoil to spread the load, and keep the top level with the coping so it cannot snag
Keep the 0.6 m setting but footing the ladder with a colleague, and extend it by one rung above the coping to give a place to grip
Move the foot about 2.4 m out to lower the risk of tipping backwards, and pack the spoil flat with bricks, keeping the ladder top level with the coping
why: A plank on loose spoil is still unstable ground, and a top level with the coping gives nothing to hold when stepping off.
A foot only 0.6 m out is too steep and may tip backwards, and one rung gives too little handhold.
A base that far out makes the ladder slide and leaves no handhold above the landing.
bank.ex: A ladder should sit at about 75 degrees on stable level ground and extend roughly a metre above the landing to give a handhold when stepping off.
bank.cm: Fixing the ladder angle while ignoring the ground beneath the feet and the handhold at the top.

bank.stem: After chasing brickwork in a small plant room, fine grey dust lies over the floor and pipework. A labourer proposes sweeping it with a dry brush while wearing a basic paper mask, saying the dust is plainly visible so it is easy to control. What is the best way to clean it?
o: Sweep dry with a soft broom after the other trades have left so nobody else breathes the cloud, and prop the door open to ventilate the room
Sweep dry but wear a half-mask respirator, since correctly fitted respiratory protection removes any need to change the cleaning method used
Use a standard household vacuum cleaner, which collects the dust without lifting it and so needs no specialist filter
Vacuum it with an industrial cleaner fitted with a high- efficiency filter, since the finest dust is invisible and sweeping lifts it again
why: This only moves the exposure to the sweeper and leaves airborne dust to settle again, so the method is still wrong.
Respirators are a last resort after controlling the source, and they do not stop dust spreading to other workers.
Ordinary vacuum filters pass the finest particles straight back out through the exhaust, so a suitable filter is needed.
bank.ex: The most harmful respirable fraction cannot be seen, and dry sweeping lifts it into the breathing zone, whereas a suitably filtered industrial vacuum captures it.
bank.cm: Judging a dust problem by what can be seen and relying on a mask when a better cleaning method exists.

bank.stem: A labourer is told to enter a manhole chamber to clear a blockage. A colleague says it is only 1.5 m deep and smells normal, so he can go straight down after opening the cover and waiting a minute. What is the best advice?
o: Enter after the wait, since a shallow chamber under two metres cannot build up harmful gas and counts as open ground
Enter wearing a dust mask and tell a colleague nearby, since a sense of smell is enough to warn of harmful air
Enter on a rope tied to his belt with a colleague holding it at the top, as this is as good as a rescue plan
Treat it as a confined space: assess, test the air, and use a safe system including a rescue plan, as a normal smell proves nothing
why: Depth does not decide the risk, as gas can collect in any chamber.
A dust mask gives no protection against gas and smell is not a reliable warning.
A person holding a rope cannot rescue an unconscious casualty and may be overcome by trying.
bank.ex: Chambers can hold toxic gas or lack oxygen with no warning smell, so entry needs assessment, testing and a rescue arrangement set up beforehand.
bank.cm: Judging a chamber to be safe by its depth or smell instead of testing the air and arranging rescue.

bank.stem: A bank is refurbishing one floor of its occupied head office through a principal contractor. A manager says CDM covers only the builders, so the bank's own staff, who share the lift lobby and fire escape, are the contractor's concern alone. Which statement is most accurate?
o: The client's arrangements must cover anyone affected, including its own staff, so it must share information on the occupied premises and co-ordinate its operations with the contractor
The client may hand every duty to the principal contractor once it is appointed, so the bank keeps no further responsibility for risks created by the works
CDM duties attach to those carrying out construction work, so the bank's staff are protected by general workplace law and the client need only appoint the contractor and pay
The client's duty covers its staff only if the project is notifiable to HSE, so below the thresholds the contractor alone must manage the effect on them
why: A client keeps its own duties and must take reasonable steps to check the arrangements are working.
Client duties under CDM extend to people affected by the project, not just construction workers.
The client's duty to make suitable arrangements applies to all projects, notifiable or not.
bank.ex: A client must make suitable arrangements so the work is done without risks to anyone affected by the project, which includes its own staff and visitors, and must pass on what it knows about the premises.
bank.cm: Assuming that appointing a principal contractor passes every client duty to the contractor, including those for the client's own occupied premises.

bank.stem: A random test on a site with a drugs and alcohol policy returns a positive result for a prescribed sedating medication taken by a crane slinger. He had told nobody. Which response best fits good practice?
o: Remove him from safety-critical duties, review the result confidentially with occupational health, and agree fitness and any duty changes first
Take no action, because the drug is prescribed and legal, and assume the doctor has already judged him fit for slinging duties on a construction site
Tell the whole gang about the result so everyone can watch for drowsiness, and keep him on his current duties under closer informal supervision
Treat it as gross misconduct and dismiss him on the spot, because any positive result breaches the policy whether or not the drug was prescribed
why: The prescriber may not know the work, and a legal medicine can still impair someone doing safety-critical tasks.
Sharing private medical information is inappropriate, and informal watching does not remove an impaired worker from safety-critical work.
A policy should distinguish prescribed medication from misuse, and automatic dismissal skips the fitness assessment the situation calls for.
bank.ex: A prescribed medicine is not misuse, but its effect on safety-critical work must be assessed confidentially by a medical professional and duties adjusted if needed.
bank.cm: Assuming that a legally prescribed medicine is automatically safe to work on, or that a positive result automatically means misconduct.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The carpenters say every truss is already nailed securely to the wall plate. What is the most significant problem?
o: The trusses stand without proper temporary bracing, and the carpenters work from the chords with no deck or fall protection
The scaffold lacks a toe board along the eaves, which is the main fault because the trusses themselves are already fixed and therefore stable enough
No roofing felt or tile battens have been fixed yet, so the trusses are exposed to the weather and should be covered before any work continues
The carpenters are not wearing harnesses, and clipping onto the trusses would solve the fall risk since the roof structure is already fixed in place
why: The trusses are not stable without bracing, so treating the toe board as the main fault misses the collapse and fall risks above it.
Weather exposure is not the pressing safety issue, since covering comes after the structure is braced and the work at height is protected.
Unbraced trusses are not a reliable anchor and could fall over with the wearer, so a harness on its own does not solve the problem.
bank.ex: Trusses must be braced as they are erected to keep them stable, and people working on them need a deck or other fall protection below, because nailing to the wall plate alone does not hold them upright.
bank.cm: Judging that a roof frame is safe to work on because each member has been nailed down, rather than because it is braced and protected.
bank.alt: Carpenters stand on the timber roof trusses of a new house, with scaffolding around the walls below.

bank.stem: A bulk diesel delivery is due at a site's 2,000-litre bunded tank, which is close to a surface-water gully. The driver will fill it while the labourer who ordered it is away, and the tank gauge is known to stick. What is the best arrangement?
o: Let the driver fill it alone, because the bund will hold any overflow and a bunded tank means no checks on the delivery are required at all
Place a drip tray under the nozzle and let the driver fill the tank unattended, as the tray will contain any drips from the nozzle
Trust the gauge and have the driver stop when it reads full, then record the volume afterwards, since the paperwork shows what was delivered to site
Check the tank's spare capacity, have a trained person present throughout, and cover the gully with a spill kit to hand before filling
why: A bund is a last line of defence, and overfilling or hose spills can still run over its edge or reach the gully before anyone responds.
A drip tray catches only small drips and does not deal with overfilling, and nobody is present to raise the alarm quickly.
The gauge is known to stick, so it cannot be relied on, and a record made afterwards will not prevent an overfill.
bank.ex: Overfilling and hose leaks are common causes of pollution, so the delivery should be matched to the capacity, supervised, and protected by drain covers and a spill kit.
bank.cm: Assuming a bunded tank makes oil deliveries safe without anyone checking capacity or watching the filling.

bank.stem: At a 60-person contractor, two trade-union-appointed safety representatives send the director a signed letter asking for a safety committee. He says he will consider it at the year-end review, and that a committee is compulsory only when the HSE orders one. Which statement is most accurate?
o: A written request from at least two safety representatives obliges him to set one up, and it must be in place within three months of the request
A committee becomes compulsory only when three representatives ask, so he may defer to the annual review and consult the representatives informally until then
The duty arises only when the trade union itself asks in writing, and the committee must then be established within twelve months of that request
He may decline if he consults the representatives and records his reasons, because the regulations leave the decision on a committee to his judgement
why: The trigger is a written request from two representatives, and the law sets a three-month limit that a review date cannot override.
The request comes from at least two safety representatives rather than the union, and the time limit is three months, not twelve.
Once two safety representatives request one in writing, establishing the committee is a duty and not a matter of employer discretion.
bank.ex: Under the Safety Representatives and Safety Committees Regulations 1977, a written request from two or more safety representatives requires the employer to establish a committee no later than three months after the request.
bank.cm: Assuming a safety committee is a favour the employer can schedule or refuse, rather than a duty triggered by a written request from two representatives.

bank.stem: A high-lift skip dumper must tip into a feed hopper. The driver, standing on a gentle cross-fall, raises the skip and edges forward the last metre to line up, saying speed saves time. Which statement is correct?
o: Raise the skip only halfway while moving, because stability falls only once the skip is fully vertical, so a half-raised skip stays within the safe limits
Creep forward in low gear with the skip raised on the cross-fall, because the danger comes from speed and walking pace removes the risk of overturning
Raise the skip only on level ground with the brake on, then lower it fully before repositioning, since a raised skip greatly reduces stability
Tip from the cross-fall if the downhill wheels sit on firmer ground, since firm contact on the low side stops the dumper from rolling over
why: Stability reduces as soon as the skip is lifted, so moving with it partly raised is also unsafe.
A raised skip on a cross-fall can overturn at any speed, and low gear does not restore stability.
Firmer ground on one side does not make a cross-fall safe, because raising the skip shifts weight and can still tip the machine.
bank.ex: A high-lift skip must be raised only on substantially level ground and never driven while raised, because stability falls sharply once the skip is elevated.
bank.cm: Believing that slow speed, or only part- raising the skip, makes it safe to move or work on uneven ground with the skip up.

bank.stem: A 30-tonne wheel loader reverses all day on a site beside houses, and neighbours complain about its high-pitched beeper. The manager wants the alarm switched off, saying a rear camera gives the driver full sight. What is the best response?
o: Keep an audible alarm but change to a broadband type that is less intrusive off site, and keep the banksman and exclusion zone because cameras leave blind spots
Switch the alarm off during early hours only, since the camera covers the rear, and ask the driver to reverse at a slower speed with extra care and patience
Fit a louder alarm and add sound baffles round the loader, so that the warning is still heard by workers wearing ear defenders on site
Replace the alarm with a flashing beacon, since pedestrians in hi-vis can easily see lights, and the beacon causes no noise nuisance to the neighbours at all
why: Cameras leave blind areas, and an alarm warns people the driver cannot see on any shift.
A louder alarm worsens the nuisance and does nothing about blind spots or the lack of segregation.
A beacon warns only people who happen to look at it, so it is not a full substitute.
bank.ex: A camera covers only part of the area around large plant, so the audible warning and banksman remain necessary, and a broadband alarm reduces the nuisance without removing the warning.
bank.cm: Assuming a rear camera makes the other warning measures redundant, even though it leaves areas around large plant unseen.

bank.stem: A caulker applies a solvent-based sealant for six hours in thin disposable gloves that show no tears. He rinses them at lunch and wears them again in the afternoon. Which approach to glove selection and use is most appropriate?
o: Match the glove material and breakthrough time to the solvent in the safety data sheet, change before that time passes, and never reuse
Wear two pairs of the same thin gloves and rinse theouter pair at lunch, because the doubled layer will block the solvent for the full shift
Switch to thick general-purpose work gloves, because thickness is what resists solvents and any heavy glove will cover him safely through a whole working shift
Keep the thin gloves because an absence of tears shows no solvent has passed through, and replace them only when visible damage appears during the shift
why: Two layers of the same unsuitable material only slow permeation slightly, and rinsing does not restore a glove that has already been affected.
Resistance depends on the glove material against the specific solvent and not on thickness, and some heavy gloves absorb solvents and hold them against the skin.
Permeation happens through intact material, so the lack of visible damage does not show that the glove is still protecting the skin.
bank.ex: Solvents can pass through a glove that looks intact, so the material must be matched to the substance, replaced within its breakthrough time, and not reused after rinsing.
bank.cm: Judging whether a glove is protecting you by how it looks and feels rather than by its material and breakthrough time.

bank.stem: On a frosty morning, a gate marshal at a vehicle entrance wears his issued hi-vis waistcoat under a dark padded parka because it is too small to go over it. He says he will unzip the parka if a vehicle approaches. What is the best response?
o: Swap the parka for a thin jacket so the waistcoat fits over it, since being cold is a matter of comfort that has no bearing on safety
Provide hi-vis weather clothing, such as a hi-vis coat or larger outer waistcoat, so the conspicuous layer is outside and he stays warm
Accept the parka if it is clean and has reflective tape on it, since the waistcoat beneath still meets the standard if unzipped in time
Let him wear the parka and add a bright chest torch, because a lit torch is a recognised substitute for hi-vis clothing at site gates
why: Cold affects alertness and the employer should provide suitable clothing for the weather as well as for visibility.
A garment hidden under a dark coat does not make him visible, and relying on him unzipping in time puts the control on a split-second action.
A torch is not equivalent to conspicuous garments that are visible from all sides and in all light conditions.
bank.ex: Cold-weather clothing should either carry suitable hi- vis features or be worn under the hi-vis garment, and the employer must supply items that fit and work in the conditions.
bank.cm: Letting workers cover their hi-vis with bulky coats because the issued vest does not fit over them.

bank.stem: Pipelayers dig a 3.5 m deep square pit in firm clay for a new manhole. They plan to dig to full depth, then climb down to fit struts and sheets from inside because the sides look stable. The pit was inspected on Monday. What is the correct approach?
o: Fit supports only to the lower half of the pit, since falling soil from above a depth of 2 m is unlikely to injure a person standing below
Fit support as the pit deepens, or place a system from the surface, so nobody enters unsupported ground, with inspection at each shift start
Dig to full depth and then fit supports from inside, because the Monday inspection covers the whole week while the clay remains dry
Climb down once the clay feels sound, since firm clay stands unsupported for as long as it has not been disturbed by vibration or weather
why: Collapse from any height can bury or crush a worker, so there is no safe depth for leaving the sides partly unsupported.
Inspection is required at the start of each working shift and after events affecting stability, not once a week.
No ground can be relied on to stand unsupported in all circumstances, so appearance and feel do not make entry safe.
bank.ex: No ground can be relied on to stand unsupported, so support must go in before people enter, and a competent person must inspect at the start of each shift and after any event.
bank.cm: Judging an excavation safe by how firm the ground looks rather than by what supports it and when it was last inspected.

bank.stem: A contractor will core-drill 150 mm holes through a first-floor slab for new ducts above a working office. The risk assessment names only the drill operator as at risk and gives 'wear PPE' as the control. Which improvement is most important?
o: Name the staff below as exposed, scan the slab for reinforcement and services, and cordon off the area underneath before any drilling begins
Keep PPE as the main control but add a second operative to watch the drill, since the office staff are outside the contractor's work area
Add only a dust and slurry control, because falling cores and hidden cables in the slab are matters for the rig manufacturer rather than for the assessment
Ask the office manager to tell staff to avoid their desks, because the occupier's own rules cover anyone who is not employed by the drilling contractor
why: A second watcher does nothing to protect people below, who remain unassessed.
Dropped cores and drilling into hidden services are foreseeable hazards that the assessment must cover.
The contractor must plan and control the risk it creates and cannot hand it to the occupier.
bank.ex: A suitable assessment considers everyone who could be harmed, including people below, and uses physical controls such as scanning and exclusion zones ahead of PPE.
bank.cm: Listing only the people doing the work when the assessment should cover everyone the work could harm.

bank.stem: A canopied air compressor stands in the corner of a concrete stairwell with its canopy doors propped open for cooling. Two plasterers work 3 m away. Which approach best reduces their noise exposure?
o: Close the canopy doors, put the compressor outside or in an open area, and use a longer hose so it sits further from the plasterers
Move the compressor closer to the plasterers to shorten the hose, as a shorter air line reduces pressure losses and so makes the machine quieter
Leave the layout as it is because the stairwell walls enclose the noise, so the sound level cannot rise beyond that of the canopy alone
Keep the doors open for cooling and issue ear defenders to both plasterers, which brings their exposure down to a safe level without moving any equipment
why: A shorter hose does not make the compressor quieter and bringing it nearer increases exposure.
Hard enclosed walls reflect sound and raise levels, which is the opposite of containing the noise.
Hearing protection is the last resort, and relying on it ignores the cheap controls that reduce noise at the source and on its path.
bank.ex: Enclosures only attenuate noise when closed, corners and hard walls reflect it, and levels fall with distance from the source, so ear protection is the last control.
bank.cm: Propping open a noise enclosure for convenience and relying on ear defenders to make up the difference.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The site supervisor says the ladder is secure because the man is using both hands and it has been set at a proper angle. What is the most significant problem?
o: The ladder top rests against plastic guttering, which cannot carry its load, so a stand-off or another form of support is needed
The man should be wearing a full-body harness clipped to the ladder rungs, since a fall from 3 m could cause serious injury without fall arrest
The base needs a second person footing it, because a ladder on paving is stable only if someone is standing on the bottom rung at all times
The ladder is set too shallow for safe use, so the base should be moved closer to the wall to reduce the chance of the ladder sliding outwards
why: Harnesses are not normally clipped to ladder rungs, which are not designed as an anchor point.
The base is on firm level paving with a stabiliser bar, so the fault in the picture is at the top.
The ladder is shown at a correct angle of about one in four, so the angle is not the problem.
bank.ex: Guttering is not a suitable support, as it may deform or crack and let the ladder slip, so a stand-off frame or a different access method is needed.
bank.cm: Checking the angle and the footing of a ladder but never looking at what the top is resting against.
bank.alt: A worker climbs a ladder against the eaves of a house while a supervisor watches from the patio.

bank.stem: A pipe rolls onto a labourer's forearm, crushing it and tearing a deep wound. Blood is pumping out and soaks through two pressure dressings within minutes. The first aider has a commercial tourniquet in the kit. What should he do?
o: Keep adding dressings and raise the arm, because a tourniquet risks the limb and should be left until a paramedic arrives to decide on it
Peel off the soaked dressings to inspect the wound, then re-dress it and press with a fresh pad before deciding on any other step
Apply the tourniquet but loosen it every ten minutes to restore circulation, which stops the limb from dying while help is on its way to the site
Call 999, fit the tourniquet above the wound and tighten until the bleeding stops, note the time, and leave it on for the ambulance crew
why: Waiting while blood continues to pump risks death within minutes, and a tourniquet is the accepted step when pressure fails.
Removing dressings disturbs clots and wastes time, and pressure has already failed to control this bleed.
Loosening the tourniquet restarts the bleeding and it should be left in place for medical staff to remove.
bank.ex: Life-threatening limb bleeding that dressings cannot control needs a tourniquet applied above the wound, and it must stay tightened and be timed so the ambulance crew know when it went on.
bank.cm: Treating a tourniquet as a last resort that must be loosened periodically, when for a life-threatening limb bleed it is left tight and timed.

bank.stem: A supplier's competent team finishes erecting a hired tower crane at 11 am. The contractor's assessment records 'competent crew, low risk', and the manager wants lifting to start at noon with the erectors choosing the operator. Which approach is correct?
o: Wait for the independent thorough examination, and check operator, slinger and lift plan for this site, since skill in erecting is not skill in using
Begin with light loads while the operator tests the controls, since that proves the crane and a written examination is needed only at the yearly interval
Start at noon, because the people who built the crane are best placed to judge it safe, and their own commissioning checks serve as the examination
Obtain the examination report, then start, because the erectors' competence also covers choosing the operator and the lifts, so no site checks follow
why: A trial lift is not an examination, and assembly at a new location triggers one before first use regardless of the yearly cycle.
The thorough examination must be done by a sufficiently independent competent person, not by the erecting team checking their own work.
Competence to erect does not show that an operator or lift plan is suitable for this site's loads, routes and signalling.
bank.ex: Equipment assembled on site needs a thorough examination after assembly and before use, and the users must separately confirm operating competence and a lift plan for their own site.
bank.cm: Treating the competence of the erecting team as proof that the crane is examined and its users are ready.

bank.stem: Look at the bricklayer on the scaffold lift. The scaffold has been inspected and tagged. What should the supervisor do before any more brickwork is laid?
o: Ask him to clip a lanyard to the top guardrail while he stands on the blocks, since this arrests any fall from the stack
Have him come down off the stacked blocks and re-site materials, so he works from the platform and the rails give proper edge protection
Accept the set-up, because guardrails and toe boards are fitted and the current inspection tag shows the protection is built into the scaffold
Have a colleague steady the blocks while he works, since the guardrails stop him falling over the edge of the platform
why: A guardrail is not a suitable anchor point, and a fall from the stack could still be over the rail.
Inspection covers the scaffold itself, not how workers then use it or raise themselves above its protection.
Holding loose blocks is not a stable base, and his raised position makes the guardrail ineffective.
bank.ex: Standing on loose blocks raises his body above the guardrail height and on an unstable base, so the rails no longer protect him from falling.
bank.cm: Judging scaffold safety from the fitted rails and the inspection tag, without checking how workers stand and use the platform.
bank.alt: A bricklayer works on a scaffold lift beside a brick wall while another worker watches from the ground.

bank.stem: In an occupied shop, a fitter asks the owner if he can plug a 110 V site transformer feeding his tools, plus a 2 kW heater, into a wall socket. The owner shrugs and says to go ahead. The fitter's leads are all PAT tested. What should the fitter do?
o: Check the socket works and the plug is fused at 13 A, then use it, since any domestic socket is built to carry two appliances at full load
Connect it only for short bursts, since an overloaded socket circuit trips its breaker well before any cable could overheat or catch fire
Go ahead, since the owner has agreed and his own PAT- tested leads and plug fuses will protect against any overload on the shop's existing wiring and its socket circuit
Have the shop's responsible person confirm the circuit's rating and protection, and a competent electrician approve the temporary supply, before connecting
why: Sockets share a circuit with other loads, so a working socket says nothing about the circuit's capacity or protection.
Protective devices on an unknown circuit cannot be assumed to trip in time, and short bursts still carry the risk.
Plug fuses and tested leads protect the equipment, not the shop's fixed wiring, whose rating and protection are unknown.
bank.ex: The shop's wiring was not installed for site loads, so its capacity and protection must be known and approved by a competent person, as a casual consent does not make the circuit suitable.
bank.cm: Treating a client's casual permission to use a wall socket as proof that the circuit is suitable for site equipment.

bank.stem: A facade scaffold stands beside a street used by schoolchildren, and the site will be shut for two days. A ladder runs from the ground to the first lift, and loose boards and a bundle of tubes lie on the bottom lift. What is the best arrangement before leaving?
o: Lash the bottom of the ladder with rope and fix a 'Keep off' sign at its base, since lashing and signage together will deter children from climbing
Leave everything in place, because a green tag showing a recent inspection means the scaffold is secure against misuse and needs no further steps
Remove the bottom ladder to a locked store or fit a padlocked guard, and clear loose boards and tubes from the lower lifts into secured storage
Raise the ladder and leave it on the first lift platform, so reaching it from the pavement would need a jump and most children would not attempt it
why: Rope lashing is easily undone and signs alone are unlikely to deter children, so neither makes the rungs unusable.
An inspection tag shows structural checks, not protection against unauthorised access or loose materials.
A ladder left on the first lift can still be reached or pulled down, so it should be removed or locked away rather than just moved.
bank.ex: Taking away or guarding the access ladder stops unauthorised climbing, and clearing loose items removes things that could be moved or pulled down onto people.
bank.cm: Assuming that an inspected, tagged scaffold is secure out of hours when ladders and loose materials remain accessible.

bank.stem: A supplier will deliver 40 kg rolls of roofing membrane and tins of solvent-based adhesive to a cramped city site on Thursday. The manager intends to decide where to unload once the lorry arrives. Which approach best controls the risks?
o: Order the smallest practical quantity and keep both materials together in the cabin, because limiting volume removes the need for a planned drop zone or store
Leave the assessment to the haulier, since the driver is responsible for the load until it is on the ground, and keep site staff away until then
Brief the driver on arrival and unload at the nearest kerb, because the delivery note shows what is on board and a single drop needs no earlier assessment or planning
Assess beforehand using the supplier's weights and safety data sheet, then plan the unloading method, a pedestrian-free drop zone and a separate adhesive store
why: Reducing the quantity helps but does not remove the manual handling or the fire risk, and flammable adhesive should not be kept with other materials in a cabin.
The site controls its own premises and must plan access, ground, storage and people, so it cannot hand this assessment to the haulier.
A delivery note is not hazard information, and deciding on the spot leaves no time to arrange safe unloading or storage.
bank.ex: Risks from materials are controlled by assessing the delivery before it arrives, using the supplier's hazard information to plan unloading, segregation and storage rather than improvising at the kerb.
bank.cm: Assuming that deliveries can be sorted out when they turn up, rather than assessing the materials before they are ordered or arrive.

bank.stem: A chain-lift skip lorry driver arrives for a large skip filled level with its sides with broken concrete and brick. It looks too heavy, but the contractor insists it is not overfilled and wants it gone quickly. What should the driver do?
o: Lift it, because material level with the sides is not overfilled and the customer who hired the skip carries the legal responsibility for the weight of its contents
Lift it a short distance to test it, then lower it and decide, since the vehicle's behaviour will show whether the chain lift is overloaded
Decline to lift it if he judges it over the vehicle's weight limit, and ask for material to be removed, since a level skip of dense waste can be too heavy
Net the load, drive carefully on minor roads to the tip, and let the weighbridge show whether it was overweight, since the tip will check it later
why: The driver and operator must not lift or carry an overweight load, whoever filled the skip and however level it looks.
A trial lift loads the chains and vehicle beyond their limits and risks failure with people close by.
Driving an overweight vehicle is unlawful and unsafe, and a weighbridge check afterwards does not make the lift or journey safe.
bank.ex: Weight, not volume, decides whether a skip can be lifted and carried, so a driver should check the load is not overweight and refuse to lift it when the pick-up seems unsafe.
bank.cm: Judging whether a skip can be lifted by how full it looks instead of how heavy the contents are. PRACTICE TEST 20

bank.stem: A firm replaces its disc cutters with new battery saws that have a different guard and kickback behaviour. The manager says experienced operators need no retraining and offers an optional toolbox talk on Saturday morning, unpaid. What does the law require?
o: Training may be held outside working hours if operators agree in writing, since a signed agreement passes the time and cost of it to the worker
Training is a legal requirement only on recruitment, so experienced staff may join a voluntary session outside their normal hours if they choose to
Experience on cutters is presumed to cover any similar tool, so handing out the manufacturer's written instructions is enough to meet the employer's duty
Operators must be trained on the new saws' risks before they use them, repeated where appropriate, and the training must take place during working hours
why: The duty to train in working hours stays with the employer and an operator's agreement cannot move it on.
Training is also required when new equipment brings new or changed risks, and it cannot be left to voluntary unpaid attendance.
Experience on the old discs does not cover the new guard and kickback, and leaflets alone are not training.
bank.ex: The Management Regulations require health and safety training when new work equipment is introduced, adapted to the changed risks, repeated where appropriate and delivered during working hours.
bank.cm: Assuming that experienced workers do not need retraining when the equipment they use changes.

bank.stem: A rotating laser level, marked Class 3R, is set on a tripod in a corridor where other trades walk, with its beam sweeping at head height. The operator says it is only a weak red line. What is the best way to control the eye risk?
o: Set the beam well above or below head height or screen it, warn other trades, and switch it off when unattended, since the blink reflex is no dependable defence
Keep the laser running all day for stability and put one warning sign at each end of the corridor, since a sign alone gives passers-by complete protection
Issue ordinary impact-rated safety glasses to everyone using the corridor, because standard eyewear filters laser light of this power and so removes any need to move the beam
Leave the beam at head height and rely on the blink reflex, since visible red light of this class always makes anyone look away before any harm occurs
why: A sign only warns and does not remove the beam from eye level, so it cannot be the sole control.
Impact eyewear is not designed to filter laser wavelengths, so it gives a false sense of protection.
The blink reflex is not guaranteed, particularly if someone stares or views the beam through optical aids.
bank.ex: Removing the beam from eye level and limiting its use controls the hazard at source, whereas the aversion reflex cannot be relied on to prevent a harmful direct exposure.
bank.cm: Assuming a low-power visible laser is harmless because it looks dim and people will blink away from it.

bank.stem: A supervisor notices a normally reliable plumber has become withdrawn, makes errors and has worked long hours on a tight deadline for weeks. A colleague says it is his own business and he should toughen up. What is the best approach?
o: Record a warning for his errors, because a formal process will motivate him to improve quality before the deadline
Move him to a lighter task without discussing it and tell the gang the reason so that they can keep an eye on him
Talk to him privately, treat work stress as a risk to assess, adjust workload and hours, and point him to support
Leave him alone since stress is a personal matter outside the employer's duties, and step in only if he asks for help
why: Discipline adds pressure and ignores the likely cause of the errors.
Telling colleagues breaches his privacy and acting without talking to him may not tackle the cause.
Work-related stress is a health risk that the employer must manage.
bank.ex: Employers must assess and manage work-related stress like other health risks, which means a private conversation, changes to workload and hours, and access to support.
bank.cm: Treating signs of work-related stress as a personal weakness rather than a hazard to manage.

bank.stem: A worker using a breaker says anti-vibration gloves let him safely work beyond the daily exposure limit value for hand-arm vibration. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Anti-vibration gloves give no reliable protection, so exposure must be controlled through trigger time, tool choice and job rotation instead
Gloves are a cold-weather measure, and a worker wearing them can safely exceed the limit because warm hands tolerate vibration better
Gloves reduce vibration enough to allow roughly double the usual daily exposure, provided they are certified to the relevant standard
The exposure limit value applies only to workers not wearing gloves, because gloved hands are treated as a separately protected group by the manufacturer
why: Warm hands help circulation, but gloves do not permit exposure above the limit values.
There is no such allowance; gloves are not a recognised way to exceed the limit.
Limits apply to the vibration exposure regardless of gloves.
bank.ex: Gloves cannot be relied on to reduce vibration to a safe level, so the control is to keep daily exposure under the action and limit values through tool choice, trigger time and job rotation.
bank.cm: Believing anti-vibration gloves are a reliable control that allows higher exposure.

bank.stem: A site's welfare facilities suited the first crew of six, but the workforce has grown to twenty and nothing has been added. The manager says welfare is only a temporary-site courtesy. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Welfare is the principal designer's responsibility only, so contractors on site have no need to review the facilities as numbers change
Welfare duties apply however short the project, and provision must be scaled to the workforce on site and reviewed as numbers change
Welfare rules only apply to projects lasting more than six months, because shorter jobs are treated as temporary work under a lighter regime
Welfare provision is fixed at the planning stage for the whole project, so extra workers must make do with what was agreed at the outset
why: Contractors and the principal contractor have duties to provide and maintain adequate welfare.
There is no such minimum duration; the duty applies from the start of work.
Provision must be adjusted when the number of workers changes.
bank.ex: Temporary sites are not exempt from welfare requirements, and facilities fixed at the start of a project must grow with the workforce.
bank.cm: Treating welfare as a one-off set-up task rather than something that must keep pace with the workforce.

bank.stem: A supervisor says a yellow triangular 'deep excavation' sign and a blue circular 'hard hats must be worn' sign are both 'just reminders' that workers can judge for themselves. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Both are advisory, because no safety sign creates a legal requirement on its own and workers are expected to judge the risk for themselves on site
The yellow triangle only warns of a hazard, while the blue circle is a mandatory instruction that must be followed, so they do not carry equal weight
Both are mandatory, because any safety sign displayed on a site must be obeyed in the same way whatever its shape or colour, with no difference in weight
The triangle is mandatory and the circle is a warning, because a triangle indicates that a specific action must be taken by the worker concerned
why: Mandatory signs indicate required actions that employers must enforce.
A warning sign informs about a hazard; it does not itself prescribe an action.
The meanings are reversed; triangles warn, blue circles mandate.
bank.ex: Sign shape and colour carry meaning: warning signs inform, prohibition signs forbid, and mandatory signs require a specific action which employers must enforce.
bank.cm: Treating all safety signs as the same level of instruction regardless of shape and colour.

bank.stem: A telehandler's forks drop a pallet of blocks beside a pedestrian walkway. Nobody is hurt, so the supervisor logs nothing and tells the driver to take more care. Which approach to the incident is correct?
o: Record it as a near miss and look for root causes such as load stacking, segregation and supervision, rather than stopping at the driver's lapse
Retrain the driver and close the matter, since human error by the operator is the root cause in nearly every handling incident of this type
Report it to the HSE immediately as a dangerous occurrence, because any dropped load must be notified whether or not anyone was injured
Investigate only if the injured person's absence reaches the reporting threshold, because near misses without harm carry no legal or practical value for the site
why: Blaming the individual ignores the system failings, such as pedestrian segregation and load security, that let the error cause danger.
Not every dropped load is a notifiable dangerous occurrence, and the point here is internal recording and investigation.
Near misses are valuable learning, and waiting for an injury means the failure is repeated first.
bank.ex: Near misses show the same failures that later cause injuries, and effective investigation looks beyond the immediate act to the underlying management and system causes.
bank.cm: Closing an incident as soon as someone has been blamed or because nobody was injured.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The supervisor says the guardrails are complete. What is the most significant problem?
o: The top rail is too low to stop a fall, so the edge protection fails and the workers above should wear harnesses as the main control instead
No toe boards or brick guards, with materials stacked at the edge, mean objects can fall onto people on an unprotected route below
The pallets of bricks are stacked too neatly, which suggests the load was moved by crane and the guardrails were removed to allow the lift
The gap between the top and mid rails is too large for a person to be stopped, so the guardrails are the main fault in the scene
why: The top rail height shown is adequate, and collective edge protection is preferred over personal fall protection.
Neat stacking is not a hazard, and nothing indicates removed guardrails.
The rails shown are correctly spaced, so the fault lies in what is missing below the rails.
bank.ex: Edge protection must also contain materials and debris, and loads stored near an edge or unprotected areas below create a falling-object risk to others.
bank.cm: Judging edge protection only by whether it stops people falling, and overlooking materials falling onto those below.
bank.alt: A scaffold with guardrails along the edge of a slab, with pallets of bricks and timber stacked on it; a worker walks along the ground beneath.

bank.stem: A steel erector walking along a floor beam 5 m above the ground clips a 2 m lanyard to a beam clamp at his foot level. The supervisor says he is attached, so it is fine. What is the main concern?
o: The anchor is acceptable because a beam clamp is always rated for fall arrest, so the height of the connection has no real effect on the outcome
A foot-level anchor lengthens the free fall, raises impact force and uses up clearance, so a high anchor or overhead lifeline should be used
The problem is only the lanyard length, so a longer 3 m lanyard fitted to the same clamp would give a softer stop and solve the issue
Lanyards should be removed completely on steel frames, since being attached to a beam makes a falling worker swing and strike the steelwork
why: Anchor height strongly affects fall distance and the forces that the body and equipment experience.
A longer lanyard from a low anchor makes the free fall and clearance problems worse.
Swing is a risk to be managed with anchor position, but it is not a reason to work unattached.
bank.ex: Anchor points should be above the user where possible, because a low anchor lengthens the fall, raises the forces on the body and may leave too little clearance.
bank.cm: Treating any attached harness as safe without checking where the anchor sits relative to the wearer and the ground.

bank.stem: An HSE inspector arrives unannounced at 06:30 as concrete pours begin. The site manager says she must book an appointment, that photographs need written permission, and that nobody will assist her until the director arrives. Which statement is correct?
o: She may enter only with a magistrate's warrant, so the manager can lawfully keep her at the gate until one is produced to him in person
She must give at least 48 hours' notice for routine visits, unless a serious accident has already happened and the HSE has been informed of it by the employer
She may enter at any reasonable time without notice, take photographs and samples, and require the manager to provide facilities and assistance within his control
She may enter without notice, but photographs and samples need the written consent of the person in control, and assistance can be held back until a director attends
why: Entry to a workplace needs no warrant, and refusing to let a warranted inspector in can itself be an offence of obstruction.
There is no notice requirement for entering a workplace, and a prior accident is not a precondition for an unannounced inspection.
Her powers to photograph, sample and require assistance do not depend on consent or on a director being present.
bank.ex: Under section 20 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 an inspector may enter at any reasonable time, take photographs, measurements and samples, and require any person to afford facilities and assistance; obstructing her is an offence.
bank.cm: Assuming an inspector needs an appointment, a warrant or the employer's consent before she can enter, photograph and ask for help.

bank.stem: Operatives lift a pavement manhole cover to pull cable, then leave the chamber open during lunch with a single cone beside it and nobody present. Which approach is correct?
o: Leave it open but keep one worker standing nearby, since a person watching the hole is as effective as a barrier while the others carry on working
Place two cones and a sign at the opening, since a clear warning and a short absence are enough where the chamber is shallow and the hole is small
String red-and-white tape between two cones around the opening, since tape creates an exclusion zone that passers-by are legally bound to respect
Fit a rigid barrier all round or refit the cover whenever the opening is unattended, because a cone gives a warning but does not stop a person falling in
why: Relying on a person's attention is weaker than a physical barrier, and it fails when that worker is distracted or leaves.
A warning is not a barrier, and the duty to prevent falls into an opening is not removed because the chamber is shallow.
Tape is a marker and cannot stop a pedestrian or vehicle entering the area or falling into the opening.
bank.ex: Openings that people could fall into must be guarded or covered so that falls are prevented, and a cone only warns, so a physical barrier or cover is needed whenever the work area is left.
bank.cm: Treating a cone or tape as if it were a barrier around an open manhole or shaft.

bank.stem: At 6:55 am a supervisor gives a gang a 14-page RAMS and asks them to sign the front sheet and start. One operative, whose English is limited, signs without reading it. A colleague says the signature now makes him personally liable. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Understanding is the operative's own responsibility, so he should ask for a translation himself and the supervisor may carry on if no questions are raised
The signature moves the legal responsibility for following the method onto the operative, so the employer's briefing duty is met once the front sheet is signed
A single briefing at induction covers every later task, so the gang need only sign again when the whole contract changes rather than for each RAMS issued
Sign-off should follow a briefing that checks each worker understands the controls, with language support if needed, as a signature alone proves nothing
why: The duty is on the employer and supervisor to check understanding, not to wait for the worker to speak up.
Signing cannot transfer the employer's duty to give information and instruction in a form workers can understand.
Task-specific methods and controls need briefing for the work in hand, and again whenever the RAMS changes.
bank.ex: The RAMS only works as a control if the people doing the task have understood it, so the briefing must be checked and adapted to the audience, and a signature is just a record of that briefing.
bank.cm: Treating a signature on the front sheet as proof that every worker has read, understood and accepted the controls.

bank.stem: A supervisor says a square brick-lined chamber, 1.5 m deep and reached from a road cover, cannot be a confined space because it is small and has a ladder. The chamber is connected to a sewer, and its air has not been tested. Which statement is correct?
o: It is a confined space only if the chamber is completely sealed, because a cover that lifts leaves it open to the atmosphere
It is not a confined space, because a fixed ladder gives a way out and a worker who feels unwell can simply climb up to the surface
It may be a confined space, because enclosed or largely enclosed places with a foreseeable risk such as toxic gas or low oxygen count, whatever their size
It is not a confined space, because the term applies only to tanks and vessels more than 2 m deep that are entered through a hatch
why: A confined space is enclosed or largely enclosed, and a lifted cover over a deep chamber still allows dangerous atmospheres to collect.
Easy exit does not remove the risk, as gas can overcome a worker within seconds before he can climb out.
There is no depth threshold and chambers and sewers are recognised confined spaces if a foreseeable risk exists.
bank.ex: The test is whether the place is enclosed or largely enclosed and has a reasonably foreseeable risk of serious injury, such as gas, fumes or lack of oxygen, not its size or depth.
bank.cm: Judging a space by its size or depth instead of by whether a serious risk such as gas or low oxygen is foreseeable.

bank.stem: The structural engineer issues a revised drawing swapping a roof steel for a heavier section. The crane lift plan and temporary works were prepared for the original. The site manager says the existing RAMS still stand because the lift is routine. What is the correct position?
o: Leave the review to the steel fabricator, because the design change is outside the contractor's control and the lift is not its own risk to assess
Review the lift plan, temporary works and assessment against the revision, coordinate through the principal contractor, and brief the crew first
Wait for the next scheduled quarterly review of the RAMS, as a routine lift only needs reassessing at set intervals on a long project
Carry on and update the paperwork once the steel is in place, since the crane's rated capacity already covers any normal steel section on a roof
why: The contractor controlling the lift must reassess its own method, and cannot hand that duty to the fabricator.
A significant change must trigger an immediate review, and fixed intervals do not replace it.
Capacity depends on radius and configuration, and reviewing after the lift defeats the purpose of planning it.
bank.ex: A design change alters the load, the crane radius and the temporary works, so the assessment must be revisited and communicated before work proceeds.
bank.cm: Treating a signed-off assessment as fixed, even after the design or site conditions it was based on have changed.

bank.stem: A joiner who has traded alone for years takes on his first full-time labourer. His policy carries 10 million pounds of public liability cover, and he says this already protects the new employee. Which statement is correct?
o: The public liability limit exceeds the legal minimum, so it can stand in for employers' liability cover if the labourer is named on the policy schedule
Employers' liability cover becomes compulsory once he has five or more staff, which is also when the certificate must be made available to them
He must hold the cover, but the certificate is a commercial document for his insurer and clients and does not have to be available to employees
He needs separate employers' liability insurance of at least 5 million pounds from an authorised insurer, with the certificate accessible to his employee
why: Public liability covers members of the public and not employees, so naming the labourer on it does not satisfy the compulsory insurance duty.
The duty applies from the first employee, and there is no five-person threshold for the insurance or the certificate.
The certificate must be accessible to employees, for example on site or electronically, and shown to inspectors on request.
bank.ex: Employers must hold employers' liability cover from the first employee, at no less than 5 million pounds, and make the certificate accessible to staff and inspectors, whereas public liability protects third parties.
bank.cm: Assuming that a large public liability policy automatically covers the people who work for you.

bank.stem: A slinger rigs a two-leg chain sling, marked 2 t up to a 90-degree included angle, to lift a 1.6 t beam with the legs spread to about 110 degrees. He says 2 t is greater than 1.6 t. What is wrong?
o: The sling should first be proof-loaded at 2 t on site, since a trial lift confirms it will take the extra tension from the wide legs.
Nothing is wrong, because the marked load applies at any angle up to 120 degrees, which is the standard maximum for chain slings in use.
The lift is fine if a second slinger checks the angle and signs the lift plan, since the plan overrides the rating marked on the sling tag.
The marked limit applies only up to the stated angle, so at 110 degrees the safe load is lower and he needs longer legs or a higher-rated sling.
why: Slings are never tested on site by trial lifts, and the correct step is to rig within the rating.
The 120-degree figure is an upper limit for use, not a statement that the rating is unchanged at every angle below it.
No plan or signature can override a sling's marked working load limit at the angle used.
bank.ex: Leg tension rises as the included angle widens, so the working load limit falls beyond the angle marked on the sling, and the rigging must be changed to keep within that rating.
bank.cm: Comparing the load only with the number on the sling tag and ignoring the angle at which that number applies.

bank.stem: Digging a foundation trench, an operator exposes dark, oily-smelling soil and a corroded drum. The foreman says to keep digging, tip the spoil on the next plot to keep to programme, and wash hands at lunch. What is the correct response?
o: Carry on unless the soil visibly reaches a watercourse, as environmental controls apply only once pollution has left the site boundary
Carry on with dust masks worn, and spread the soil on the next plot because moving it around the same site avoids waste rules
Lift the drum out, then bury it deeper in the trench and backfill over it, so the contamination is not left exposed to rain or workers
Stop digging, keep people clear and report it so the soil is assessed before any leaves, with hygiene controls for those exposed
why: Duties to prevent pollution apply before it escapes, and worker exposure risks exist whether or not water is affected.
Unassessed contaminated soil moved on site can spread pollution, and masks do not control skin contact or vapour.
Concealing the drum risks leaving a pollution source and breaks duties to assess and dispose of hazardous waste properly.
bank.ex: Unexpected contamination must be investigated and classified before disturbance or removal continues, to protect workers from exposure and prevent it spreading to other ground or water.
bank.cm: Pressing on with excavation when something unexpected turns up in the ground because stopping would disrupt the programme.

bank.stem: Site pedestrians cross a haul road at a corner where stacked cabins block the view of approaching lorries. The manager's only action is a 10 mph sign at the gate. Which approach best controls the risk?
o: Open up the sight lines, mark a barriered pedestrian crossing, and back up the speed limit with physical measures
Leave the cabins where they are and fit a convex mirror at the corner, as a mirror lets drivers and pedestrians see each other clearly
Keep the sign and rely on drivers sounding the horn at the junction, since an audible warning is enough to protect anyone crossing
Station a banksman at the gate to check speeds, since the traffic is restricted to site speed once vehicles are inside the entrance
why: A mirror gives a limited view and does not remove the blind corner or separate people from traffic.
Horn sounding is a weak warning that depends on drivers and pedestrians hearing it and acting in time.
A banksman at the gate cannot control speed or movements at the blind corner further inside the site.
bank.ex: Good traffic management removes the blind spot, separates pedestrians from vehicles at a defined crossing, and enforces speed with physical measures instead of relying on a sign alone.
bank.cm: Relying on a speed sign alone to protect pedestrians when the layout still hides them from drivers.

bank.stem: A bricklayer foreman needs more space at a window reveal and tells his labourer to shift a ledger and a transom on the facade scaffold, saying it is only two tubes and he will refit them tonight. What is the most accurate response?
o: A labourer may make minor changes provided the tubes go back by the end of the shift and the foreman checks them by eye afterwards
Moving tubes within a single bay is allowed if a second person holds them in place, since the only risk is from falling objects
Only competent scaffolders should alter it, and it must be inspected again before use, as the missing members could weaken the whole scaffold
Alterations are fine if the bay is closed to workers overnight, because a scaffold is only loaded while people are working on it
why: Competence for scaffold work is required, and a foreman's visual check is not a formal inspection of the altered structure.
Holding tubes is no substitute for competence, and the main risk is the loss of the structure's stability.
A weakened scaffold can still fail in wind or under its own weight, even when nobody is on it.
bank.ex: Scaffolds are designed as a whole, so alterations must be done by competent scaffolders and the scaffold inspected before use to confirm it remains stable and safe.
bank.cm: Treating a couple of scaffold tubes as a small thing that anyone can move and put back.

bank.stem: At finish, a driver parks a forward-tip dumper facing downhill on a sloping track beside the cabins, handbrake on, engine off, with the skip still raised from the last tip. He says the handbrake alone will hold it. What is wrong?
o: Nothing is wrong, because a parking brake is designed to hold a machine on a slope and the raised skip only helps rain drain away
He should leave the engine running in gear, so the transmission also holds the machine, which is safer than shutting it down
The skip should be lowered, but chocks are needed only on public roads, because the brake secures plant on private land
The brake alone is not enough, so the machine should go on level ground away from routes, or be chocked, lowered and keyed off
why: A raised skip is an extra hazard, since it raises the centre of gravity and can drop or be struck, and the brake is not a sole control.
Leaving a machine running and unattended invites unauthorised use and fuel and noise problems, and creates a hazard rather than a control.
Chocking is a precaution for any slope on any site, and the duty to secure plant does not depend on who owns the ground.
bank.ex: A parking brake can fail or be released, so plant is parked on level ground where possible, and on a slope it is chocked with the skip lowered and the key removed so it cannot be moved.
bank.cm: Trusting the parking brake alone to hold plant and leaving it on a slope with the body raised.

bank.stem: A man buys a terraced house to let out and pays one builder to refit its kitchen and bathroom before the first tenants arrive. He says he is a domestic client because he owns the house personally, so the builder holds his client duties. Which statement is correct?
o: He is a domestic client because the house is in his own name, so the single builder takes on his client duties automatically under CDM 2015
He is a commercial client but may pass every client duty to the builder verbally, because a single contractor can take on the role
Work done for a letting business makes him a commercial client, so he keeps the full client duties and cannot hand them to the builder
He becomes a commercial client only once tenants have moved in, so until then the builder carries the client duties as a default
why: Personal ownership does not decide the status, because the work is for a letting business and not for his own or a relative's home.
Commercial client duties cannot be passed on by a verbal agreement, and they remain with the client who commissions the project.
The purpose of the work, not the date a tenant arrives, decides his status, and the work is already being done for a business.
bank.ex: A domestic client is someone having work done on their own home or a family member's home, not as part of a business, so a property being refitted to let is a commercial client's project.
bank.cm: Assuming that owning a property personally makes you a domestic client, whatever the reason the work is being done.

bank.stem: After four hours digging in cold rain, a labourer is soaked, drowsy, confused and slurring his words. A colleague suggests sending him to the cabin alone for a hot shower. What is the most appropriate action while help is called?
o: Add extra layers over his wet clothing and let him carry on digging, since heat from steady exercise will bring his body temperature back up
Rub his arms and legs briskly to restore circulation and give him a small measure of spirits to warm him from the inside quickly
Call 999, move him to shelter, remove his wet clothing, wrap him warmly including his head, and stay with him talking until help comes
Let him take a hot shower to rewarm quickly, then rest unobserved so he can recover in privacy, calling help only if he is no better later
why: Wet clothing keeps drawing heat from his body, and a confused worker needs to stop work and get medical help.
Rubbing limbs and giving alcohol are both advised against in hypothermia, as they can make his condition worse.
Hot baths or showers are not advised for hypothermia, and someone confused must not be left alone or have emergency help delayed.
bank.ex: These are signs of hypothermia, which needs emergency medical care, and the safe interim steps are shelter, removing wet clothes, gentle insulation and continuous observation.
bank.cm: Treating confusion and slurred speech in a cold, wet worker as tiredness that he can work off rather than as a medical emergency.

bank.stem: A tipper driver is told to discharge hardcore under a temporary pipe gantry 5 m up, on soft ground that slopes slightly sideways after rain. He says the raised body will clear the pipes by half a metre. Which assessment is correct?
o: Tip as planned because pipework, unlike power cables, cannot electrocute anyone, so only the slope matters and a slow tip deals with that
Tip as planned but with the driver standing well back from the cab holding the controls, which would protect him if the lorry became unstable
Do not tip there, as the raised body can foul overhead pipework and tipping needs firm level ground, so move to a clear, level area first
Tip in stages with a banksman watching the clearance, since he can warn the driver in good time to lower the body before it touches anything
why: Overhead pipework is also an obstruction that a raised body can strike, so the area must be clear of it as well as cables.
The driver should stay in the cab with the doors closed during tipping, not stand outside where an unstable body could fall on him.
A banksman cannot correct soft, sloping ground, and instability can develop faster than any warning can be given.
bank.ex: A tipping site must be clear overhead of pipes and cables and firm and level, as a raised body on a slope can become unstable and swing into obstructions.
bank.cm: Judging a tipping position only by whether the raised body is expected to miss obstructions, without checking the ground is firm and level.

bank.stem: A principal contractor locks the welfare cabin and takes the site rules off the gate on Saturdays, saying none of its own staff work then. A subcontracted electrician works alone one Saturday with its agreement. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Site rules matter only when several trades overlap, so a lone worker needs just a portable toilet and a mobile phone for emergencies
Welfare must be available throughout the construction phase to everyone working there, and the electrician must still follow the site rules
The electrician's own employer must arrange toilets and washing, because the contractor's duty covers only its own staff on its planned working days
A lone worker needs no welfare provision for one day, because facilities become mandatory only once a minimum headcount is on site
why: Site rules are part of controlling risk throughout the project and apply to every worker, however few are present.
The principal contractor's welfare duty extends to all workers on the site, not just its own people or its normal days.
The duty to provide facilities does not depend on a headcount threshold being reached on a particular day.
bank.ex: The principal contractor must provide suitable welfare facilities for the whole construction phase and keep site rules in force, so a lone subcontractor on a quiet day is covered by both.
bank.cm: Assuming welfare and site rules only matter on days when the main workforce is present.

bank.stem: Halfway through construction, the client asks for a lighter roof beam to be substituted for the specified steel one. The structural designer issues a revised drawing by email to the site agent. The principal designer says the change is a site matter now. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Liaison ended when the pre-construction phase finished, so the revised drawing only has to be filed with the health and safety file at handover
The designer must consider the risks the change creates and pass on the information, while the principal designer keeps liaising with the principal contractor
The designer may issue the revision without further information provided the new beam meets the structural calculations and the client has approved it
The change is an alteration to the construction method, so only the principal contractor must assess it once the original design has been signed off
why: Liaison with the principal contractor continues for the duration of the principal designer's appointment, not just until construction starts.
Structural adequacy and client approval do not remove the duty to address health and safety risks from the change or share information about them.
A design change is still design work, so the designer's duties to address foreseeable risk and provide information remain in force.
bank.ex: Designers keep their CDM duties for design changes made during construction, and the principal designer must liaise with the principal contractor and share relevant information for the length of the appointment.
bank.cm: Assuming design responsibilities stop once construction begins, so later changes are treated as purely a site matter.

bank.stem: Look at the scene. The operative is wearing high-visibility clothing, a helmet and safety boots. What is the most significant problem with how this work is set up?
o: The operative should face the traffic at all times, since he could then see any vehicle approaching and step clear in good time
The saw is being used at kerb level, which is the main hazard, because cutting low produces more dust and requires respiratory protection first
There is no proper signing, guarding or separation from the moving traffic, so the work zone itself does not protect him
Traffic noise will stop him hearing the saw, so hearing protection is the most urgent missing item, before any change to the traffic arrangements
why: Watching traffic is not a control, as a vehicle at speed leaves no time to react, and it removes his attention from the saw.
Dust is a real concern but it is secondary to the risk of being struck by passing vehicles a metre away.
Hearing protection is a separate matter and would not address the risk of being hit by a vehicle.
bank.ex: High-visibility clothing is a last line of defence, and work beside a live carriageway needs planned signing, guarding and physical separation so that traffic cannot reach the working area.
bank.cm: Relying on bright clothing and personal vigilance to deal with traffic when the work area itself has not been properly signed and separated.
bank.alt: A worker kneels at the kerb cutting with a petrol saw beside a live road, with two traffic cones and approaching vehicles.

bank.stem: A contractor boasts 300 days without a RIDDOR-reportable injury and trims site inspections to save time. A review finds weekly inspection actions overdue, lapsed training records and very few supervisor observations. What is the soundest conclusion about measuring performance?
o: A low injury count is a lagging measure; overdue actions and lapsed training are leading indicators of weakening controls, so both kinds need monitoring
The overdue actions matter if the HSE asks for them, because RIDDOR data is the measure the law uses to judge whether a site is managed well
The injury record proves the controls are working, so inspections can be reduced further until an injury occurs and shows a problem needs attention
The injury record is the most reliable measure, because inspections and training records describe paperwork and cannot show whether controls are actually working in practice
why: The law requires risks to be managed, and RIDDOR reporting is not a test of performance, so ignoring open actions is a management failure.
Waiting for an injury to signal failure defeats the purpose of prevention and ignores the evidence of weakening controls.
Active checks reveal control failures before harm occurs, and a short injury record can reflect luck rather than good management.
bank.ex: Lagging measures such as injuries only record failures after the event, while leading indicators show whether controls are being maintained, so relying on either alone gives a misleading picture.
